articles.headline: Golden State Valkyries reach WNBA Finals: How second-year franchise made unprecedented run
keyFacts: The Golden State Valkyries advanced to the WNBA Finals by sweeping the Las Vegas Aces with an 87-77 overtime victory.
Driven by a strong defensive performance, the expansion franchise reached the championship series in just their second season.
The Valkyries will face the Atlanta Dream in the WNBA Finals beginning on October 17.
body: Just over three years ago, on Oct. 5, 2023, the Golden State Valkyries were officially introduced as the WNBA's first expansion team in over a decade. At the introductory press conference, more than a year before the team even had any players, let alone took the court for the first time, team owner Joe Lacob made a bold proclamation.

"First press conference with the Warriors, I said we will win a championship in the first five years," Lacob said. "I'm telling you right now, we will win a WNBA championship in the first five years of this franchise."

After completing a sweep of the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces on Friday with a thrilling 87-77 overtime victory in Game 3 of the semifinals, the Valkyries have advanced to the WNBA Finals for the first time in franchise history and are four wins away from making Lacob look like a genius. They'll face the Atlanta Dream in the WNBA Finals, beginning on Oct. 17.
Put this in your bookmarks. @wnbagoldenstate owner Joseph Lacob vows that once play begins, they will win a championship in the first 5 years of their existence 🙌 pic.twitter.com/Xxa5limkMz
— WNBA (@WNBA) October 5, 2023

The Valkyries made history in their inaugural season in 2025 when they set a record for wins by an expansion team (23) and became the first expansion franchise to make the playoffs in their inaugural season. Despite the initial success, expectations weren't high entering 2026, especially after a somewhat confusing offseason highlighted by trading their first-round pick (Flau'jae Johnson) for two second-round picks.

But the Valkyries' strong belief in their internal development proved well-founded, and they were bolstered by the arrival of free-agent signings Gabby Williams and Kiah Stokes, who helped make their defense so overwhelming that it made up for their continued issues on the offensive end.

The Valkyries didn't have a single player average more than 15 points per game, finished seventh in offensive rating (108.2), which was the second-worst mark of any playoff team, and were 13th in true shooting (54%), above only the Seattle Storm and Connecticut Sun, the two worst teams in the league.

But on the other end, the Valkyries had one of the best defenses in WNBA history. Their 99.1 defensive rating was more than four points per 100 possessions better than any other team, and they finished second in both opponent true shooting (53.5%) and opponent turnover rate (19.2%).

Their defensive-minded approach carried them to a 32-10 record -- a nine-win improvement on last season -- and the No. 2 seed in the playoffs. It almost cost them in the first round, however, when they shot 35.1% in a winner-take-all Game 3 against the Dallas Wings, and had to pull off a stunning 16-point comeback to keep their season alive.

Their offense was a bit better against the Aces, but once again, their defense stepped up to save the day. The Aces were 3-0 against the Valkyries in the regular season, in large part because A'ja Wilson and Jackie Young did whatever they wanted in those contests. Those two were held in check in the semis. Wilson had 23 points per game on 41.1% shooting, while Young put up just 14.3 points on 31.6% from the field. As a team, the Aces' true shooting was 50.8% -- nearly 10 percent worse than their 59.3% mark in the regular season.

During the series-clinching victory on Friday, the Valkyries completed an 11-point comeback in the second half in large part because they held the Aces to just two points over the first eight minutes and 25 seconds of the third quarter. Las Vegas went just 2 of 16 from the field in that frame.

Williams, who made her second All-Star appearance this season and finished as the runner-up to Angel Reese for Defensive Player of the Year, averaged 20.3 points to lead the way in the series, while Kayla Thornton put up 14 points and Tiffany Hayes chipped in 11.7. As a team, the Valkyries shot 39.8% from the field, had a true shooting mark of 54% and barely had more assists (41) than turnovers (40). And yet, they're going to the Finals.
We've simply never seen an organization or a team like the Valkyries.

articles.headline: Dricus Du Plessis believes he could fight for the title next
keyFacts: Dricus Du Plessis stated he believes he could fight for the middleweight title next following his recent win over Kamaru Usman.
Du Plessis noted that the middleweight division is in a weird situation regarding who receives the next title shot.
Sean Strickland wants to transition into boxing and is currently in stalled negotiations over money, according to the article.
body: Former middleweight champion Dricus Du Plessis captured the 185-pound title at UFC 297 in January 2024 by defeating current titleholder Sean Strickland via spit decision. He dominated Strickland in their rematch at UFC 312 .

“Stillknocks” lost the belt to Khamzat Chimaev in one-sided fashion at UFC 319 but rebounded from the loss in his last outing by soundly defeating former welterweight champion Kamaru Usman . With the win, and considering the landscape in the weight class, Du Plessis believes he could fight for the title next.

“After the last fight, I just prove again that I can be the best in the world and that I will be the best in the world. Where we are at right now is continuing building on those blocks that we built before that fight. Looking at what’s next, I mean, time waits for no one. Right now, they’re obviously going to do Strickland and [Nassourdine] Imavov . I think the middleweight division is in a bit of a, it’s a weird situation because who gets the next title shot? And I’m 100% ready for that,” Du Plessis told Fight Forecast .

In light of Strickland’s recent comments about wanting to transition into boxing and a willingness to give up the 185-pound title, the top of the middleweight division is at a standstill. Strickland wants more money and judging from his social media posts, negotiations aren’t going well.

“I had an injury. I was out for a while, but I told them I would be ready to fight early next year. It’s interesting because I don’t know what they’re going to do. Who are they going to make me fight? They’re not going to make me fight backwards. And right now we have Strickland, Imavov, Khamzat and myself. So, It’s going to be interesting,” continued the South African.
“You’re as good as your last fight. Obviously I last a bout. I was off 11 months working on everything to be the best in the world again. I have no doubt that I will be champion again.”

articles.headline: Thousands of security personnel deployed as Delhi braces for ‘cockroach’ protest
keyFacts: Delhi authorities deployed over 30,000 security personnel and blocked roads after denying permission for a major protest on Saturday.
Protesters led by the Cockroach Janata Party demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign over voter roll manipulation allegations, which officials deny.
Movement founder Abhijeet Dipke said the group will march to the Jantar Mantar protest site on Saturday despite police bans.
body: - Published

Parts of the Indian capital, Delhi, have been turned into a fortress, with tens of thousands of security forces deployed, as the influential Gen Z-led "cockroach" movement has called for a major protest on Saturday.
The protesters are seeking electoral reforms and the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of manipulating voters' lists.
The Election Commission has denied this and Kumar is yet to comment on calls for his resignation.

The protest comes just months after the movement brought thousands of young people onto Delhi's streets in July, in demonstrations that saw violent clashes with police and forced India's education minister to resign.
Police say they have denied permission for Saturday's gathering, and all roads leading to Jantar Mantar, the main protest venue, have been closed off with huge metal barricades.
The restrictions have caused major disruption across central Delhi, with traffic diverted from several key roads. A journey that would normally take 15 minutes took more than an hour this morning.
At Jantar Mantar, police and paramilitary personnel are stationed behind barricades and ropes, preventing people from entering the protest site. Drones could be seen flying overhead.
Some protesters who arrived early were stopped and questioned by security personnel. The BBC also saw at least five people being detained near the site.
Journalists covering the protest have been cordoned off into a designated area nearby.
At a nearby roundabout, loudspeakers repeatedly broadcast appeals for people to cooperate with the police.
Delhi Police has defended the measures, saying they were necessary to maintain public safety and prevent overcrowding at Jantar Mantar, which can accommodate only 1,000 people at a time.
Several trains to Delhi have also been cancelled and police have ordered dozens of metro stations shut to prevent protesters from gathering.

But Abhijeet Dipke, founder â of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) - the online satirical movement that is spearheading the protests - has said the CJP will march to Jantar Mantar on Saturday morning "come what may".
"If you want to jail us or even shoot us we are prepared," he added, addressing âPrime Minister Narendra Modi in a post on X.

The CJP first emerged as a major protest movement during weeks of demonstrations demanding education reforms over the summer. The resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan in July was seen as a major victory for the group.

CJP protesters returned to the streets last week with a rally in Mumbai to demand Kumar's resignation. On Thursday, they held another large rally in the southern city of Bengaluru (formerly Bangalore).
Student groups and opposition parties have also protested in the capital over the past few days.
Saturday's protests are being billed as the biggest in recent times as they are also being supported by several opposition parties, farmer organisations and student groups.
CJP leaders allege the authorities have been preventing many of their supporters from reaching Delhi.
In the capital, more than 30,000 police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed and authorities have appealed to citizens to stay away from protests.
Police official Nupur Prasad told a press conference, external that one of the reasons for denying permission to protest at Jantar Mantar was the "short notice" given by the CJP.
"Under current guidelines, an application to organise an event at Jantar Mantar must be submitted at least 10 days prior to the scheduled date," she said.
Also, she added that in the past, the CJP had not followed "lawful directions" given to them.

"In light of the non-compliance with prescribed procedures, the failure to adhere to past legal directions, and the current state of public safety, law and order, and traffic regulation, permission for the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar is hereby denied."
The CJP have questioned police denying them permission for the protest - they say that legally they only have to inform the police and do not need their approval to gather.
At the centre of the row is a controversial revision of the country's electoral rolls known as the Special Intensive Revision, or SIR, which began last year.
The Election Commission says it is to remove duplicate and ineligible entries - and so far, 130 million names have been struck off the voters' list.

But opposition parties and activists have alleged that many of those are eligible voters and that the process is being manipulated by CEC Kumar to favour Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) during elections. Both the BJP and the Election Commission have rejected the accusations.
The past few days have also seen a major escalation in the opposition's standoff with the Election Commission.
For three days in a row starting Tuesday, Delhi witnessed dramatic scenes with police breaking up protests by opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and other MPs over the issue.
Videos showing police forcing Gandhi on to a bus and preventing him from climbing out of the bus window subsequently went viral on social media.

articles.headline: Time to rise? Ranking European football's sleeping giants
keyFacts: BBC Sport selected 10 European football clubs with rich histories and large fanbases that currently compete outside their respective top flights.
The ranked sleeping giants include former champions and cup winners such as Bursaspor, Dynamo Dresden, Kaiserslautern, and Sampdoria.
Several of these clubs are currently undergoing stadium developments, ownership changes, or promotion pushes to return to elite competition.
body: - Published
Deportivo, Parma, Hamburg. Not just a football hipster's holiday hit-list, but a sample of erstwhile headline acts who have returned to their respective top flights in recent years.
You can throw Leeds United, Nottingham Forest, Schalke and Malaga into the mix too.
But with such footballing royalty back in the big time, where can you find Europe's current sleeping giants? Which one-mighty sides are still snoozing?
We first need to establish some criteria - history, heritage, fanbase, stadium. Clubs with huge potential who currently exist outside the top flight.
Calling a big city home helps, but it is not a deal-maker - sorry to fans of Bristol City and second-tier Russian outfit FC Ufa, where the local population tops one million.

Likewise, some clubs with good-sized stadiums have not made the cut. Bari, whose Stadio San Nicola is the third-largest in Italy and was built for Italia '90, stands out, though some of their calcio colleagues outside Serie A also have grounds of more than 30,000 - Hellas Verona, Messina and Palermo among them.

There's a plethora of ex-Premier League teams with top-flight worthy arenas and storied pasts, while Germany is stacked full of historic clubs with huge homes who arguably deserve a spot - Fortuna Dusseldorf, Wolfsburg, Hannover 96 - but we can't include them all.

A sleeping giant must have experienced some element of former glory and Pro Vercelli are the obvious candidate there, winning seven Italian titles by 1922. But, despite being under new ownership, the third-tier side boast neither the ground nor local population to awaken that historic status any time soon.

The other nuance is, that success cannot have come too recently. West Ham, for example, won a European competition three years ago, Wolves are recent top-flight regulars; likewise Stade de Reims, twice European Cup runners-up, and eight-time French champions Nantes.

Leaving out Steaua Bucharest was another big call. European Cup winners 40 years ago and Romania's most dominant club, they now play in Liga II. But, following a deeply divisive split, many of the traditional fanbase follow top-flight FCSB. So who really owns that legacy?

And there was a case for Boavista, title winners in 2001 but whose existence now hangs by a thread. Facing financial ruin, despite fans' best efforts, they have been ejected from Portugal's professional leagues.
Anyway, let's get on with this. Piped through the matrix above, here are my top 10 European sleeping giants - you can have your say in the comments, too.
10. Bursaspor
League titles: One (2009-10). Domestic cups: One (1985-86). Division: 1.Lig, second tier. Stadium: Centennial Ataturk Stadium (43,361)

Historically dominated by Istanbul's elite teams, Bursaspor snapped that long-running streak by becoming only the second club from outside of the capital - and first since Trabzonspor almost three decades earlier - to clinch the Turkish title in 2010.
That meant Champions League nights against Manchester United and Rangers, but in 2024 the Green Crocodiles dropped into the fourth tier for the first time in their history.

Based in a city of about 2.5m people - Bursa sits in the north west, south of Istanbul, near Mount Uludag - and with a unique crocodile-shaped stadium that can house 43,361 fans, Bursaspor have soared up the pyramid since and are looking to return to the Super Lig for the first time since 2019.
9. Dynamo Dresden
League titles: Eight (most recent East German DDR-Oberliga 1989-90). Domestic cups: Seven (most recent 89-90). Division: 2.Bundesliga, second tier. Stadium: Rudolf-Harbig-Stadion (32,085).

Without wanting to turn this into a 2.Bundesliga table, this is the first of four German entries. But Dynamo Dresden, bearing a complex history and situated in the underrepresented east, feel a little different.

Initially enjoying the support of the security forces before their best players were relocated to Berlin, Dynamo became European regulars and lost to Liverpool in the Uefa Cup in 1976 and European Cup two seasons later.

One of East Germany's most dominant clubs, they won eight titles and seven cups and joined the Bundesliga in 1991 following reunification, but they dropped into the third tier four years later amid relegation and mounting debts.
Dynamo, with alumni including Matthias Sammer, have bounced around the regional and lower leagues for many years but now sit in 2.Bundesliga.
Based in a city of more than half a million people, their potential is underpinned by a large, passionate fanbase who averaged over 30,000 for home games in the second tier last term.
8. Kaiserslautern
League titles: Four (most recent 1997-98). Domestic cups: Two (most recent 95-96). Division: 2.Bundesliga. Stadium: Fritz-Walter-Stadion (49,327)

With their 1997-98 success, Kaiserslautern remain the only side to win the Bundesliga immediately after promotion, albeit following a surprise relegation having also been champions in 1991 and enjoyed cup triumphs in 1990 and 1996.
European regulars in the 1990s and early 2000s, it is now almost 15 years since they competed in the Bundesliga, spending four seasons in the third tier before a promotion in 2022.

Despite modest league finishes, the club continue to record average crowds of more than 46,000 and almost pulled off another shock in 2024 when they reached the German Cup final, losing to Xabi Alonso's Leverkusen.
7. Sheffield Wednesday
League titles: Four (most recent 1929-30). Domestic cups: Four (most recent 90-91). Division: League One, third tier. Stadium: Hillsborough (39,732)

Sheffield United fans may argue that they, not city rivals Sheffield Wednesday, should make this list. But the Owls edge it on history and heritage - even if the most recent of their four league titles came almost 100 years ago.

Wednesday were League Cup winners in 1991, and in living memory for many gave us magical moments from the likes of David Hirst, Chris Waddle and Paolo di Canio. Yet they now sit in the third tier after entering administration and enduring relegation last season, before a US consortium bought the club in May.
The Owls, boasting England's 12th biggest club stadium, were relegated from the top flight in 2000, but fans are fuelled with fresh optimism that a reawakening is possible.
6. Hertha BSC
Leagues: Two (most recent 1931). Domestic cups: Two (most recent 2002). Division: 2.Bundesliga, second tier. Stadium: Olympiastadion (74,475).
I'm convinced Hertha have huge potential, if not the history to match some of their counterparts. Their only titles, for example, precede the Bundesliga era.
But the Old Lady once reached a Uefa Cup semi-final and beat Chelsea in the Champions League in 1999.

This season is their fourth consecutive campaign outside the top tier, but Hertha continue to play at Berlin's Olympiastadion and regularly attract more than 50,000 fans. A new ground on the Olympic Park site, housing up to 52,000, is being considered.

Currently top of 2.Bundesliga, Hertha can tap into a deep talent pool on their doorstep - highly rated youngsters Ibrahim Maza and Kennet Eichhorn have joined Leverkusen, goalkeeper Tjark Ernst went to Feyenoord - and look equipped to return to the Bundesliga in fine shape.
5. Bordeaux
Leagues: Six (most recent 2008-09). Domestic cups: Seven (most recent 12-13). Division: Regional 1, sixth tier. Stadium: Stade Atlantique (42,115)

Bordeaux's recent troubles have been well documented. Relegated from Ligue 1 in 2022 before administration meant they tumbled into the fourth tier, this summer they were again demoted to the regional sixth tier because of financial issues.
Having seemingly hit the bottom, the 2009 French champions now at least have something to build on after being bought by US investment fund Park Bench for one euro.

Les Girondins are dripping in history. Once home to former greats Jean Tigana and Zinedine Zidane, as well as current France internationals Aurelien Tchouameni and Jules Kounde, their decade-old home hosted a Euro 2016 quarter-final - albeit Bordeaux are not playing there at present as they try to shape their future.
4. FC Nuremberg
League titles: Nine (most recent 1967-68). Domestic cups: Four (most recent 06-07). Division: 2.Bundesliga, second tier. Stadium: Max-Morlock-Stadion (50,000).
Perhaps it's not overly imaginative to be opting for the current top two in Germany's second tier but FC Nuremberg meet all the selection criteria laid out above.
They have the history - nine titles, with the latest of four cup triumphs coming in 2007; a 50,000-seater home; large local fanbase in a one-club city - and the heritage.
They're nicknamed 'Der Club' because of their status in early German football.
Oh, and World Cup winner and Germany's all-time top goalscorer Miroslav Klose is their boss.
3. Real Zaragoza
Domestic cups: Six (most recent 2003-04). European: Cup Winners' Cup (1994-95). Division: Primera Federacion, third tier. Stadium: La Romareda (under reconstruction but projected 43,000).

David Seaman, look away now. Arsenal fans of a certain vintage will remember former Spurs boy Nayim's long, looping winner beating the moustachioed stopper in the final minute of extra time to give Real Zaragoza the Cup Winners' Cup.

There have been two Copa del Rey triumphs, European journeys and star names since - Pablo Aimar, Diego Milito and David Villa among them - but three decades later, Los Manos find themselves in Spain's third tier.

Ander Herrera, aged 37, is back at his boyhood club, who are in the process of developing a new 43,114-capacity stadium for the 2030 World Cup, in an attempt to help the fallen giants return to former glories.
"Real Zaragoza belong to Europe, they belong to compete for trophies, to be fighting with the biggest clubs in Spain and in Europe," said Herrera.
2. Saint-Etienne

League titles: 10 (most recent 1980â81). Domestic cups: Seven (most recent 2012â13). Continental: European Cup runners-up (1975â76). Division: Ligue 2, second division. Stadium: Stade Geoffroy-Guichard (41,965)
Saint-Etienne were, until Paris St-Germain overtook them in the past decade, the most-decorated club in France with 10 league titles in 25 seasons from 1956-57 to 1980-81.

Les Verts reached the European Cup final in 1976, losing to a vintage Bayern Munich side, while their last silverware came in the now-defunct Coupe de la Ligue 13 years ago with a team spearheaded by Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang.

They are presently spending their fourth season in five in the second tier, but they continue to produce top prospects. Star defenders William Saliba and Wesley Fofana came off the production line, while 18-year-old attacking talent Djylian N'Guessan will join Liverpool in January.

Then there is their 41,965-capacity Stade Geoffroy-Guichard home, nicknamed the 'cauldron', which was a whisker from seeing Ligue 1 football again this term - Les Verts lost to Nice in the promotion/relegation play-off, meaning the wait to rejoin France's elite continues.
1. Sampdoria

League titles: 1990-91. Domestic cups: Four (most recent 93â94). Continental: Cup Winners' Cup (89â90), European Cup runners-up (91-92). Division: Serie B, second tier. Stadium: Stadio Luigi Ferraris (33,205)
Sampdoria were once continental big-hitters, not merely domestic champions during a golden era of Italian football.

Buoyed by Paolo Mantovani's investment, the Genoa outfit won the Coppa Italia four times between 1985 and 1994, clinched the Scudetto in 1991 and reached three European finals, winning the Cup Winners' Cup in 1990 a year after losing to Barcelona in the final.
In 1992, the team of Gianluca Vialli, Roberto Mancini and Gianluca Pagliuca were again beaten by Barcelona in extra time of the European Cup final at Wembley.

More big names followed in the period between Sven-Goran Eriksson's side winning the club's last major trophy in 1994 and a first relegation five years later - Clarence Seedorf, Juan Sebastian Veron and Ariel Ortega included.
Samp had spells back in Europe before finishing bottom of Serie A in 2023 amid serious financial problems and almost dropped into the third tier.

Under new ownership, though, fans hope the club's future is more stable - and the architecturally iconic Stadio Luigi Ferraris home they share with rivals Genoa is set to undergo an expensive redevelopment before Italy host Euro 2032.

articles.headline: Taiwan president says defence spending boost aims to ‘deter war’
keyFacts: Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te said raising defense investment aims to deter war rather than provoke, in a National Day speech.
China claims Taiwan as its territory, and Lai said Beijing applies military pressure to alter the status quo across the Taiwan Strait.
Taiwan is now waiting for United States President Donald Trump to sign off on 14 billion dollars worth of weapons.
body: Taiwan’s President Lai Ching-te has said the island “cherishes peace” and will “not give up our freedom” in a National Day speech outside the Presidential Office in Taipei.
Lai made the remarks on Saturday before thousands of people, including foreign diplomats.
“We are open to exchanges, but will not accept subordination,” he said. “Our aim by increasing investment in national defence is not to provoke; rather, it is to deter war.”
Taiwanese fighter jets and two Chinook helicopters carrying giant Taiwan flags flew over the capital ahead of the speech.
The holiday marks the 115th anniversary of a 1911 uprising that toppled China’s last imperial dynasty and led to the founding of the Republic of China.
Pressure from China

Taiwan’s 23 million people live under the constant threat of an attack by China, which insists the island is part of its territory, has never renounced the use of force to take it, and calls Lai a “separatist”.
Beijing has rebuffed his offers of talks.
Lai said China continued to “apply pressure through military and grey-zone activities in an attempt to alter the status quo across the Taiwan Strait”.
Grey-zone tactics are actions that stop short of open war. “Peace cannot rely solely on wishes, and tolerance cannot become a pretext for aggressors to encroach ever further,” he added.
Lai’s government has set aside a record 1.1 trillion New Taiwan dollars ($34.5bn) for defence in 2027, more than 3 percent of gross domestic product.

China held war games around the island shortly after Lai’s first National Day speech in 2024, but not last year. Its last drills near Taiwan were in late December, after news of an $11bn arms deal with Washington, the largest ever US weapons package for the island.
Lai said he welcomed talks between the United States and China, but insisted “there must be respect for the right of the people of Taiwan to exist”.
He urged democracies in the Indo-Pacific to join forces to preserve peace and stability in the region.
The US switched official diplomatic relations from Taipei to Beijing nearly 50 years ago but remains Taiwan’s most important security backer.
Officials in Washington and Taipei have repeatedly said US policy on Taiwan has not changed under President Donald Trump.
In May, after meeting Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, Trump suggested arms sales to Taiwan could be a bargaining chip with China, which set off alarm across the world.
Taiwan is now waiting for Trump to sign off on $14bn worth of weapons, including the US-made Patriot air defence system.
The dispute dates back to China’s civil war, when the nationalist forces of Chiang Kai-shek retreated to Taiwan in 1949 after defeat by Mao Zedong’s communists.
The Republic of China remains the island’s formal name.

articles.headline: Golden State Valkyries vanquish Las Vegas Aces to reach WNBA finals in second season
keyFacts: The Golden State Valkyries defeated the Las Vegas Aces 87-77 in overtime to complete a three-game series sweep.
The victory advances the second-year expansion franchise Valkyries to the WNBA finals.
The Valkyries will face the Atlanta Dream in Game 1 of the finals on 17 October in San Francisco.
body: Gabby Williams scored eight points in overtime as the Golden State Valkyries completed a three-game sweep of the defending champion Las Vegas Aces with an 87-77 road victory on Friday, advancing to the WNBA finals in only their second season as an expansion franchise.
After a Golden State run in the final three minutes of the fourth quarter forced overtime, the Valkyries outscored the Aces 16-6 in the extra period to secure the series in convincing fashion.

“Obviously it feels good, especially to beat the defending champs,” Golden State’s Kiah Stokes said. “They’re a team that can get hot real quick, and I think we didn’t want this to go to Game 4, Game 5, because like I said, they’re defending champs. They’ve been in this position, you don’t really want to give them any life.”

The second-seeded Valkyries will face the fourth-seeded Atlanta Dream, who clinched a finals berth with an 85-83 road victory over the New York Liberty on Friday to complete their own sweep. Game 1 of the finals is scheduled for 17 October in San Francisco.
Trailing 69-63, the Valkyries went on an 8-0 run and took a 71-69 lead on a basket from Veronica Burton with 1:12 remaining in regulation.

Las Vegas’s Jackie Young tied the game at 71 on a layup assisted by Chelsea Gray with 26.6 seconds left. After Williams missed a layup attempt with five seconds remaining, Gray’s 15ft shot at the buzzer narrowly rimmed out.
The Valkyries opened overtime with a 12-2 run that featured eight points from Williams, establishing an 83-73 lead with 46.9 seconds remaining.

Kayla Thornton led the Valkyries with 18 points and nine rebounds, shooting five of 12 from the field and six of seven from the free-throw line. Williams added 16 points on six-of-16 shooting, while Hayes and Stokes scored 11 apiece.
Stokes shot five of five from the field, grabbed 10 rebounds and played effective defense against Aces star A’ja Wilson.

“I can get emotional talking about [Kiah],” Williams said. “Honestly, she’s just someone that is so appreciated by us. Everything she does, she just knows how to win. There’s a reason she’s a three-time champion. I’ve said it a million times. ... Offensively, the way she sets screens, the way she moves without the ball, the way she gets all these offensive boards and extra possessions. Defense, I don’t think I have to say anything. We know who she is.”

Wilson, who won her record fifth WNBA most valuable player award this week, led the Aces with 21 points and 10 rebounds but shot just six of 19 from the field. Young added 16 points on six-of-16 shooting, while Gray finished with 17 points and a team-high five assists. Gray also committed a game-high six turnovers.

“If you want to win championships, you need to be a top-three, top-four defense, and we weren’t this year,” Aces coach Becky Hammon said. “We weren’t. We had moments where we were pretty good, but we weren’t good enough to be at a championship level. You got to be clicking on all cylinders on both ends, and we were not.”

articles.headline: Apple Watch Ultra 4 vs Garmin Fenix 9 Pro: Both watches nailed my accuracy test
keyFacts: TechRadar tested the accuracy of the Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Garmin Fenix 9 Pro during a thirty-minute run.
Both smartwatches and a chest-mounted heart rate monitor measured average heart rates within two beats per minute of each other.
The author stated the Apple Watch offers better software, while the Garmin features a longer battery life and survival tools.
body: The Garmin Fenix 9 Pro and Apple Watch Ultra 4 are two of the best (and most expensive) smartwatches to come out this year. But just how accurate are they?

Much has been made of Apple's redesigned Health Sensing System, supposedly the most accurate ever on a wearable. It certainly measured my sleep well enough, and Apple says it tested its accuracy by pitting it against an electrical heart rate monitor — which, funnily enough, is my process for reviewing smartwatches too.

I set out to find out how accurate Apple and Garmin's best smartwatches were by putting them against each other in a head-to-head battle, wearing them both during a 30-minute run, one on each wrist. To create a benchmark, I wore an ECG-capable electrical heart rate monitor on my chest, just like Apple's own tests; I used the Frontier X2.
The 30-minute run was more challenging than usual, because it was a very hilly route with a long incline as the midpoint — it certainly made my heart rate spike.

The figure I'm most interested in during these tests is average heart rate. I recognize that different companies use different processing algorithms, so you'll never get a 1-1 match on all heart rate data points: all you can look for is consistency in your wearable of choice, and to make sure it's generally telling the same story as a benchmark-level tool such as a chest-mounted electrical HRM, which are generally more reliable than LED-based sensors.
The closer the average heart rate, calculated by the wrist-based LED-using wearables, can get to the average heart rate calculated by the electrical HRM, the better.

Generally, I classify under 5 bpm of difference as an insignificant margin of error, meaning that's a device I'd happily keep using and recommending to others. Under 10 bpm is generally fine for light or occasional exercisers for general trends, but not one I'd recommend to fitness buffs who care about things like heart rate zones.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Anyway, on to the results — how did the Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Garmin Fenix 9 Pro stack up?
The results
The results were excellent. It’s really cool to see the Frontier X2 heart rate monitor, Garmin Fenix 9 Pro and the Apple Watch Ultra 4 all within two beats per minute of each other on average.
From left to right in the screenshots above, the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro measured 159 bpm, while the Apple Watch Ultra 4 measured 160 bpm. The Frontier X2 measured 158 bpm.

All the devices being within 2 bpm of each other is a wonderful indication of accuracy across the board. Algorithmic processing differences aside, all three devices are telling the same story about my body during that 30-minute session of exercise.
Other metrics between the two watches are similar, too. Calorie counts for example, which can vary wildly between devices, look similar as both devices estimate a burn in the high 300s — 388 vs 375.

The Frontier X2 also estimates a calorie count that's very different than the watches, but I'm discounting that as the watches collect far more information to draw from. I'm only trusting its heart rate numbers.
So, I'm more than happy with the ratings I got from these watches, and can continue to recommend them as extremely accurate health and fitness tracking tools.

So, which do I prefer? Even though both watches are very accurate, they're tailor-made for serious sports and endurance, and they're both packing dive modes and satellite communication features, they're not quite made equally.

The Apple Watch's software, third-party apps and smartwatch functionalities far outshine the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro, while the Garmin watch is built with a longer-lasting battery (10 days vs Apple's 48 hours) and features more survival tools, such as the LED flashlight.

If you're a multi-day adventurer type, I'd opt for the Garmin every time, but for day-to-day wear and shorter excursions, the Apple Watch is nicer to use — even if, unfortunately it'll need a charge every other day.

A former staffer at Men's Health, he holds a Master's Degree in journalism from Cardiff and has written for brands like Runner's World, Women's Health, Men's Fitness, LiveScience and Fit&Well on everything fitness tech, exercise, nutrition and mental wellbeing.

articles.headline: Kamala Harris’ husband, Doug Emhoff, doesn’t want her running for president in 2028: report
keyFacts: Doug Emhoff privately told people he prefers Kamala Harris not run for president in 2028, the Wall Street Journal reported.
Donors have warned Harris against running after her 2024 defeat, although she leads recent hypothetical 2028 Democratic polls.
Harris said she has not decided on running in 2028 and is focusing on 2026 midterm get-out-the-vote efforts.
body: Kamala Harris has reportedly been getting pushback about launching a 2028 presidential bid – and even her husband, Doug Emhoff, doesn’t want to see her run for the White House again.
Emhoff has privately told people that he would prefer for his wife to stay out of the 2028 presidential race, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday.
However, people close to the former second gentleman expect him to be supportive if she ultimately decides to run, according to the outlet.
Harris’ doubters extend beyond those living under the same roof as her.
Some donors – uneasy about what Harris is planning on doing – have told her directly that a 2028 White House run would be “a long shot.”
The former vice president is coming off a dismal 2024 election performance against President Trump.
Harris lost the popular vote, Electoral College and every swing state to Trump last cycle, despite raising an eye-popping $1.5 billion toward her doomed candidacy.
However, the former vice president still leads the hypothetical Democratic field by double-digits in virtually every recent 2028 poll.
Harris maintains she has not made a decision on whether to mount a third run at the presidency, but appears to be laying the groundwork for another White House campaign.

Ahead of the midterms, Harris has made the rounds at Democratic fundraisers, including private events for Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate David Crowley and Nevada gubernatorial candidate Aaron Ford, according to the Wall Street Journal.
Just last week, Harris hopped on a call with the Democratic National Committee and more than 2,000 volunteers, urging them to help with the get-out-the-vote effort in a dozen states.
“I have not decided if I’m going to run again,” she said at a NAACP event in Michigan last month. “I do sincerely believe ’28 won’t matter if we don’t get through ’26.”
Some Harris allies who have known and worked with the former vice president are “skeptical” she’ll run for president again.

articles.headline: India: Delhi braces for Cockroach protest amid strict curbs
keyFacts: Delhi police detained Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and around 500 other people to prevent a planned protest against India's chief election commissioner.
Authorities deployed about 43,000 police and paramilitary personnel, implemented internet blackouts, and restricted transport to block demonstrations over controversial voter list revisions.
Protesters and opposition parties are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the removal of millions of names from electoral rolls.
body: What you need to know
- Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke to land in New Delhi shortly ahead of protest over alleged voter list manipulation
- Around 43,000 police and paramilitary personnel are deployed in the capital, reports say
- Traffic and transport disruptions are expected
Here is our rolling coverage of developments from India on Saturday, October 10:
'Cockroach Party' founder Abhijeet Dipke has been detained

Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has been detained by Delhi police, Indian media reported, as a preventative measure to block the planned protest against India's election chief in central Delhi.

According to reports by several media outlets, including India Today, authorities detained Dipke on board a flight after he landed in Delhi on Saturday morning. The news outlet quoted Dipke as saying, "I'm not afraid of you," while police officers urged him to cooperate.
The CJP's X handle soon released footage of the detention. "Shame on you Narendra Modi, Amit Shah," the caption read, referring to India's prime minister and home minister, respectively.
Authorities have also detained CJP's co-conveners Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, as well as the group's legal aid head, Ratna Singh.
The preventative arrests are part of a major crackdown on protesters this weekend.
Most of central Delhi, where the government is headquartered, is under an internet blackout and riddled with barricades, which authorities are using to identify and stop potential protesters.
BJP calls CJP, INDIA bloc 'anarchists'

Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) National President Nitin Nabin held a press conference in New Delhi, denouncing the CJP and opposition party protests over voter list irregularities as an attempt to "create a highly dangerous and serious situation in the country."
He described the INDIA bloc of opposition parties and the Cockroach movement as "two anarchic groups."
"Your 'anarchist competition,' vying to see who can create more instability in the country, will not succeed," Nabin said, accusing both groups of "a plot to destabilize the country."
"I want to say that you are undertaking these efforts, driven by your political agendas, at the behest of foreign forces," he said without elaborating on who the foreign forces were.
YouTuber Dhruv Rathee has been detained, reports say
Popular YouTuber Dhruv Rathee has been detained by the police ahead of the Jantar Mantar protest, according to the CJP and Indian media reports.
"Dhruv Rathee has been detained. The Dictator is TERRIFIED of young people who question its wrongdoings and refuse to stay silent," the CJP wrote on X, referring to Prime Minister Modi.
According to reports, Rathee was detained at his home in Gurugam. Earlier this week, the CJP officially launched Rathee as part of its "fight to save democracy" campaign.
The Germany-based YouTuber participated in a CJP protest in the southern Indian city of Bengaluru on Thursday.
CJP legal head Ratna Singh is also reported to have been detained at her home in New Delhi on Saturday.
Hundreds of Cockroach protesters detained, says police
The Delhi Police has said in a statement that around 500 people were detained on Saturday as they arrived for the protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party, news agency ANI reported.
Around 500 people coming in different groups from various locations have been detained," ANI quoted the statement from Delhi Police as saying.

The police added that 50 more people were arrested separately and described them as "anti-social elements with criminal antecedents" who had been picked up to "so that they do not disturb" public order or "incite trouble."
Visuals aired by Indian news channels earlier showed police in central Delhi chasing young protesters before forcing them into vehicles and taking them away.
India protest: Why do protesters want Gyanesh Kumar to resign?
After India's education minister, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) movement has Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in its crosshairs.
Here is a ten-point breakdown of the controversy surrounding the top election official:

- The protests concern a contentious, nationwide voter-verification exercise — called the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) — which began last year. Around 130 million names have been removed so far from electoral rolls under the process.
- Kumar heads the three-member Election Commission of India (ECI) overseeing the SIR process.
- Last Month, The Indian Express newspaper published a report alleging differences within the ECI over decisions related to the SIR.

- According to The Indian Express, Kumar's two fellow election commissioners raised at least 14 formal objections over a 10-month period regarding voter registrations, deletions and restorations, as well as control of electoral roll data, but their concerns were allegedly not taken into consideration

- The report said that in one objection, one of the commissioners complained that the ECI had acted against the written advice of two commissioners and claimed its action was "unauthorized and illegal."
- The report sparked a political storm with protests calling for Kumar's resignation, for allegedly undermining the poll body’s credibility.
- The ECI has maintained that all its decisions were lawful, saying that differing views were a routine part of the decision-making process.
- Kumar is yet to address the allegations against him.
- Opposition leaders and critics say that those removed from the voter lists include a large number of minority voters.

- They accuse Modi's BJP of using the exercise as a tool to secure future electoral gains and question the ECI's independence. The ECI says the SIR removes deceased, relocated and duplicate voters and helps prevent the inclusion of "foreign illegal immigrants."
Delhi police detain people at protest — ANI
Police have already detained some protesters who had started gathering at Jantar Mantar for the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) protest, ANI news agency reported.
On Friday the Delhi Police said that Section 163 of India's criminal procedure law had been enforced in the New Delhi area, prohibiting all forms of assembly or protest.
Meanwhile, Indian news agencies reported that police had heightened security across the capital on Saturday, with flag marches and mock drills being conducted at several locations.
Entry and exit gates at several metro stations have also been closed, according to reports.
ANI also reported that spike strips had been deployed to deter protesters from moving through certain areas.
WATCH — Will Cockroach protest 'Season 2' take off?

The protest is being dubbed by some as "Season 2" of the Cockroach movement in India. The first wave of protests culminated with the resignation of India's education minister over exam irregularities, a rare concession by Prime Minister Narendra Modi's BJP party.
DW's Shalu Yadav takes a closer look at how the Indian government is preparing for CJP's latest protest call in this report:
CJP's Abhijeet Dipke set to arrive in Delhi

The Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) founder, Abhijeet Dipke, was due to land at Delhi's main airport on Saturday morning as the movement plans to hold a mass protest calling for India’s Chief Election Commissioner to step down over sweeping voter roll revisions, despite being denied permission by police.

Police and paramilitary forces, which local media reported numbered around 43,000 personnel, were deployed ahead of the protest. Multiple layers of yellow metal barricades blocked the concrete-grey roads leading to the Jantar Mantar protest site.
On Friday, authorities also ordered the closure of more than 50 metro stations and canceled many trains bound for two major railway stations in the capital.
But India's top court later directed the government to not completely halt train services and said there should be no blanket closure of metro stations.
The Supreme Court stressed the "principle of proportionality," urging authorities to allow the transportation services in a regulated manner to avoid public inconvenience.

"Take measures only to the extent necessary to prevent them. But that does not mean you should use a hammer to kill a fly. That principle must be kept in mind," legal news website Bar and Bench reported the court as saying.
On Saturday, Dipke denounced the Modi government over extensive restrictions.
"Modi has accepted defeat even before our protest has begun," the CJP chief wrote on X ahead of his arrival in the capital.
"The mass crackdown on protesters and the shutdown of Delhi are not signs of strength, but of a leader terrified of his own people."
Election protests: Pressure mounts on poll chief, challenge to PM Modi
The CJP is not the only group calling for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.
India's bloc of opposition parties, led by Congress' Rahul Gandhi, has been carrying out a sustained campaign against Kumar in recent days with its own protest marches.

The country has seen dramatic visuals emerge from Delhi's key corridor of political power, which showed leading opposition MPs, including Gandhi, being carried away to detention buses by uniformed police officials as they tried to dig their heels in.

The ire against India's election chief — the head of India's independent Election Commission — is turning into one of the biggest public and political challenges for Modi in his three-term rule. Opposition and critics allege that a mass deletion of tens of millions of voters from India's electoral rolls benefits Modi's Prime Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), a charge the party denies.
Welcome to our coverage!
This is Dharvi Vaid Dhulia from DW's studio in New Delhi and this is a special edition of our daily India news blog.
As the early morning hours tick away, a countdown to a rally against India's top poll official over alleged voter list irregularities has begun in the heart of the world's largest democracy.
What's happening?

India's 'Cockroaches' are headed once again for Jantar Mantar — the same protest site where the online satirical movement sprung to the mainstream as a youth-led pressure group in July after it forced the resignation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's then education minister.

The police have denied the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) permission to hold the demonstration but the group's leaders are heralding people from all over the country to converge at Jantar Mantar, calling the protest a "fundamental right".
A showdown between police and protesters seems imminent.

New Delhi, particularly its central areas, have essentially been turned into a fortress with a heavy security blanket — including thousands of paramilitary personnel — a rare mobile internet blackout, train cancellations and warnings from the police against any protest assembly.

The security arrangements come as memory is still fresh of a clash between youth demonstrators and police during the July Cockroach protest. Police used batons, tear gas and pellet-firing shotguns to disperse the agitating crowd. Several injuries were reported as the protesters alleged police brutality, while the police said it used force only after the protests stopped being peaceful.
We bring you all this and more. Stay with us as events unfold.

articles.headline: Trump calls Nobel committee’s decision an ‘indelible stain’ on Norway: ‘A disgraceful and embarrassing decision’
keyFacts: The Nobel committee awarded the Nobel Peace Prize to Navi Pillay for significantly enlarging the scope and impact of international law.
Donald Trump criticized the committee's choice, stating that awarding Pillay instead of him was an indelible stain on Norway.
Trump argued he deserved the award, claiming he stopped eight wars and saved more lives than anyone in history.
body: President Donald Trump decried the Nobel committee’s decision to award the Nobel Peace Prize to Navi Pillay, saying the decision disgraced Norway as a whole.

Speaking at a rally in Syracuse, New York, Trump went on a lengthy tangent over the decision to give his coveted prize to someone else. He began by denigrating Pillay’s lack of name recognition, calling her a “mystery person.”
President Donald Trump speaks at a campaign rally at the Oncenter, Friday, Oct. 9, 2026, in Syracuse, New York. (AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson)
“Today they gave out the Nobel Peace Prize to a person … I never heard of the person. Nobody did. It’s a mystery person,” he said.
Trump went on to pitch his own eligibility for the prize, going through the eight wars he claims to have stopped.
“Think of it. Any one of these eight wars, you get the Nobel Prize. I did eight. No president’s ever done any,” he complained.
The president also tied it into the two ongoing conflicts dominating the news cycle, saying he was “about to settle or win two more: Iran and Russia.”

He raised his candidacy for the award by claiming he had “saved more lives than anyone in history” since he prevented Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon, which the country would use to blow up “the entire Middle East, and ultimately far beyond the Middle East.”
He also noted that the 2025 winner, Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, offered to share her award with Trump.
That moment was not lost on Pillay, who joked on Friday she “may share this prize with Trump” if her supporters “clap a little bit more,” according to reports.

Trump maintained he had the stronger Nobel resume than Pillay, but, despite his “unbelievable accomplishments, the Nobel Prize was given today to a liberal person of the United Nations,” who hadn’t stopped any wars, he said.

Instead, Trump says he “should have received the Nobel Peace Prize, but didn’t. And this is an indelible stain on the country of Norway, and those people that made such a disgraceful and embarrassing decision. The Nobel Peace Prize has been forever discredited by a handful of radical ideologues who are anti-democracy, and really enemies of civilization.”

“And we will not forget, Norway, that you didn’t give this prize [to the candidate] with the greatest record in history. Not eight wars. We should have had eight Nobel Prizes for each war, but that you didn’t give the Nobel Prize for Peace to the United States of America. It’s just another sign of how Norway and all these others are ripping off our country,” the president concluded.
UN WHISTLEBLOWER ACCUSES NOBEL WINNER OF BEING ‘COMPLICIT IN THE UYGHUR GENOCIDE’

Trump’s quest for the Nobel Peace Prize has helped define his foreign policy in his second term. His refrain of “solving” eight wars has become one of his most repeated statements, and got him nominated by many different leaders, including the prime minister of Pakistan.

The Nobel committee said Pillay was awarded the prize for her role in having “significantly enlarged the scope and impact of international law.” She made headlines last year for leading the U.N. committee that ruled Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, a highly controversial decision.

articles.headline: Pokémon Go Zorua Community Day event guide
keyFacts: Pokemon Go is hosting a Zorua Community Day event on Saturday, Oct. 10 from 2-5 p.m. featuring Unovan Zorua.
Evolving Zorua into Zoroark until 9 p.m. teaches it the fast move Sucker Punch.
Event bonuses include tripled catch XP, doubled catch candy, and three-hour Incense.
body: Pokémon Go is having a Zorua Community Day event on Saturday, Oct. 10 from 2-5 p.m. in your local time. This Community Day only features the original Unovan Zorua, not the normal- and ghost-type Hisuian Zorua.
As a reminder, Zorua will initially appear as whatever Pokémon is set as your buddy. Once you catch it, it'll transform back into a Zorua, similarly to Ditto.
As expected with a Community Day event, Zorua will spawn in huge numbers with a high chance for it to appear shiny. There are also several other bonuses and perks, which we've listed out below.
How do I catch a shiny Zorua?

As per old research by the now-defunct website The Silph Road (via Wayback Machine), shiny rates on Community Days are about 1 in 24, which means that if you keep playing throughout the three-hour window, you should find quite a few shiny Pokémon.

If you're short on time or Poké Balls, you can pop an Incense, then quickly tap each Zorua to check for shiny ones, running from any that aren’t shiny. Notably, any Zorua you've already tapped will face where your player is standing, so that should help identify which ones you may have already checked.
What Community Day move does Zorua's evolution learn?
If you evolve Zorua into Zoroark from 2-9 p.m. in your local time, it will learn the fast move Sucker Punch.

If you miss out on evolving it during this period, you will likely be able to evolve it during a Community Day weekend event in December to get Sucker Punch. If you don't want to wait, you can use an Elite TM to get the move.
How does Zoroark do in the meta?
Zoroark is not great in any form of content, whether its PvE (raids and gyms) or PvP.
You can set it up with Sucker Punch and Foul Play if you want, but you shouldn't really bring this into your raids or into PvP.
How do I make the most of Zorua Community Day?
The following bonuses will be active during Zorua Community Day:
- Tripled XP for catching Pokémon
- Doubled candy for catching Pokémon
- Doubled chance for level 31+ trainers to get XL candy from catching Pokémon
- Incense lasts three hours
- Lure Modules last 1 hour
- Zorua special photobombs when taking snapshots
- One additional special trade
- Stardust cost halved for trading
That said, you should definitely pop a Lucky Egg and an Incense and try to nab some powerful Zorua.
If you can Mega Evolve Gyarados, Houndoom, Tyranitar, Sableye, Sharpedo, Absol, Greninja, or Malamar, you’ll score additional Zorua Candy per catch.

Also, if you're hunting for excellent throws for a Masterwork Research or one of the higher level requirements, you may want to consider setting your buddy to a Pokémon with a large catch ring during this event. We recommend something like Snorlax, Wailmer, or Gourgeist, but you can use whatever you're good at landing excellents on.
Additionally, if you're sick of the Zorua "Oh?" animation, you can skip this by setting a Zorua as your buddy, allowing you to make faster catches. Quick catching will also bypass this animation.

Scopely Explore is also continuing the "Lure Module Bonus" it's been running for the last year. From 2-9 p.m., Zorua will spawn in high numbers from placed Lure Modules. Even after the Community Day ends at 5 p.m., you can still find a shiny Zorua (or one with a Special Background) from lures with the increased Community Day shiny rate.
