articles.headline: Elon Musk intensifies attack on Ambani over Starlink India launch delay
keyFacts: Elon Musk accused billionaire Mukesh Ambani of blocking Starlink from launching in India and wielding outsized control over the government.
India's Ministry of Communications rejected Musk's allegations, stating that Starlink is undergoing standard security assessments alongside other operators.
Starlink's launch in India remains delayed while it awaits final regulatory approval to begin commercial operations.
body: As SpaceX struggles to launch Starlink in India, Elon Musk has stepped up his attack on billionaire Mukesh Ambani, mockingly calling him the country’s “prime minister” to suggest he wields outsized control over its government and accusing him of blocking the satellite internet service from competing.

On Friday, Musk continued his criticism of the famed Reliance Industries’ chairperson in a post on X, arguing that Starlink could bring internet access to areas that remain unconnected, giving children more opportunities to learn, and helping small businesses reach customers worldwide.
“Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?” Musk wrote.
Reliance Jio, Reliance Industries’ telecom arm, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Musk’s latest comments follow his accusations earlier this week that unnamed “oligarchs” were blocking Starlink’s launch in India to protect their business interests. India’s Ministry of Communications rejected the allegations, saying the country’s regulatory framework for satellite communications is “fair and non-discriminatory.” Musk then went further on Thursday, questioning Ambani’s influence in a separate post on X. “Is Ambani the real boss of India?” he asked.

SpaceX has spent years trying to launch Starlink in India. Last year, it even struck distribution agreements with Ambani’s Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel, India’s second-largest telecom operator, to offer the service once it received the necessary approvals. However, Starlink has not yet received the go-ahead from New Delhi to begin commercial operations, despite securing key regulatory clearances.

In its Thursday statement, the Indian communication ministry said Starlink and two other licensed satellite operators are undergoing security assessments that must be completed before they can receive satellite spectrum. The ministry said all three are at “broadly the same regulatory stage,” rejecting Musk’s suggestion that Starlink was being singled out.

Jio and Airtel are also seeking to launch their satellite internet services in India. Jio has a joint venture with Luxembourg-based SES, while Airtel is a major shareholder in Eutelsat OneWeb, which is striving to offer satellite connectivity in the country.

India, the world’s most populous country with over a billion internet users, is a major market for Musk. But expanding there also means dealing with powerful business figures such as Ambani, whose Reliance conglomerate owns India’s largest telecom operator and works with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government on major projects.

Alongside Starlink’s delayed launch, Musk has also faced challenges expanding Tesla in India. The electric carmaker launched in the country last year after years of anticipation but registered just 699 vehicles in its first 12 months of deliveries, according to data cited by Electrek. Steep import duties pushed the Model Y’s launch price in India to nearly twice its U.S. price. Tesla lowered its prices earlier this year, but its cars remain considerably more expensive in India than in the U.S.

Before Musk’s latest attack, Starlink and Ambani’s Reliance Jio clashed over how to allocate satellite spectrum in India. Musk’s company wanted the spectrum to be assigned through an administrative process, while Jio pushed for an auction. Ultimately, New Delhi went ahead with Starlink and decided to allocate the spectrum administratively.

Starlink’s launch in India remains in limbo. India’s telecom minister Jyotiraditya Scindia on Friday pushed back against Musk’s allegations, saying the country “does not allow a monopoly in any sector.”

articles.headline: Trump pledges to partner with Blakeman to ‘straighten out’ New York crime, illegal immigration and energy prices: ‘I’ll be there within 24 hours’
keyFacts: President Trump pledged at a Syracuse rally to help Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman address crime, illegal immigration, and energy prices if he defeats Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul.
Trump claimed that New York has released criminal illegal aliens with charges and convictions for over 48,000 crimes under current policies.
Blakeman vowed to end New York's sanctuary state status and open the state up to fracking to lower energy bills if elected.
body: SYRACUSE, N.Y. — President Trump on Friday pledged to immediately help Bruce Blakeman slash energy prices and crackdown on crime and illegal immigration New York, if Empire State voters choose the Republican gubernatorial candidate over Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul in November.

“Kathy Hochul and the radical ‘Dumocrats’ have turned New York into a national embarrassment of high cost, high crime, massive corruption and communist politicians chasing jobs and businesses and wealth … out of the state,” Trump said at a packed rally in Syracuse.
“The people of New York need to clean house in Albany on November 3rd, starting with Kathy Hochul,” he demanded.
Trump rattled off eye-popping statistics on the number of “migrant criminals who have been arrested” in the state, only to be set lose by Hochul “to prey on innocent New Yorkers.”

“In less than two years, New York has released criminal illegal aliens with charges and convictions for over 48,000 crimes,” he said. “These are the people that are just released into the streets, including 8,600 assaults, 1,600 robberies and thousands and thousands of rapes and kidnappings and murders.
“Democrats sanctuary policies always put innocent lives at risk.”

Trump praised the “heroes of ICE” involved in Thursday’s shooting of suspected migrant gang member Oscar Belgal in the Bronx. The president described Belgal as a “man with a criminal record a mile long who was wanted for possible murder and murder in a gang … He’s a very dangerous man, and they got him.”
“But instead of being praised,” Trump lamented, “ICE was scorned by New York politicians who set him loose.”

“If you want to stop illegal alien criminals from being released into your communities, you must elect Bruce Blakeman and a Republican Congress and we will ban sanctuary cities and sanctuary states at long last,” he promised.

Trump continued, “And if Bruce Blakeman, as your governor, calls me to help straighten out in New York City or pretty dangerous parts of this state that I know and love so much, I’ll be there within 24 hours, Bruce.”

With Blakeman in the governor’s mansion, the president declared that “within two months you’ll go from a high crime city to almost no crime at all — just like I did in Washington D.C., Memphis and New Orleans.”
Trump also raked Hochul over the coals on the high cost of electricity in the state — and said Blakeman would bring prices down by up to “90%.”

“Your energy bills are the highest in the nation. I hate to tell you that,” Trump said. “And when Bruce gets in, you’re going to go from the highest in the nation, I believe, to among the lowest in the nation — because he’s going to tap into your oil.“
“You are sitting on some of the greatest oil reserves anywhere in the world, and you’re not allowed to touch it,” he continued.
“If Bruce Blakeman gets in, he will cut your electric bills by 70%, 80% and 90%.”
The rally was held at the Syracuse OneCenter, a massive convention center in the middle of the city.
At the top of his remarks, the president fired up the crowd, saying it’s great to be back in upstate New York.
“Here we are, not far from the shores of Lake America,” he said to wild applause of the renaming of Lake Ontario.
Joining Trump aboard Air Force One for the Syracuse trip were boxing legend Mike Tyson and New York Yankees President Randy Levine.
“He’s a very dangerous person actually,” Trump bragged of Tyson.
Energy Secretary Chris Wright, EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin and New York GOP Reps. Claudia Tenney and Nick Langworthy also traveled with Trump on the presidential plane.
Ahead of the president’s speech, Blakeman warmed up the crowd by pledging that New York would be opened up to fracking and cease being a “sanctuary state” if elected.
“We’ve got to tap into that Marcellus Shale. It’s drill baby drill,” Blakeman said.

The Nassau County executive slammed Hochul as “the most pro-criminal governor in America” and said Albany policies like cashless bail and sanctuary cities are “all designed to let criminals get out and suffer no consequences for committing crimes in our communities.”
He also blamed Hochul for Thursday’s ICE shooting in the Bronx for allowing “illegal migrants with criminal records to prey on the people of our state,” Blakeman said.
“He tried to run the ICE agents over,” Blakeman continued. “Kathy Hochul, we’re outraged that you would let this guy into our state and defend him.”
Blakeman received thunderous applause when he vowed to sign an executive action declaring, “New York is no longer a sanctuary state,” if he beats Hochul.

articles.headline: Trump rallies New York crowd for Republican Bruce Blakeman's bid to replace Gov. Kathy Hochul
keyFacts: President Donald Trump rallied supporters in Syracuse to support Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman and other GOP candidates ahead of the midterms.
Trump criticized Democratic Governor Kathy Hochul over taxes, utility bills, and public safety while promoting his administration's economic and immigration agenda.
Republican candidate Bruce Blakeman joined Trump onstage to promise tax and utility cuts, improved public safety, and business-friendly policies.
body: President Donald Trump returned to his home state of New York on Friday night, showcasing America's "New Golden Age" and promising to help Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman flip the Empire State red as the GOP makes its final push toward November's midterm elections.

Trump rallied supporters in Syracuse with a sweeping celebration of his administration's economic and immigration agenda, pledging to help New Yorkers secure lower taxes, cheaper energy and safer streets by electing Republicans up and down the ballot.
"We're in the Golden Age of America," Trump told the crowd, urging supporters to deliver the same enthusiasm that powered his presidential campaigns.
TRUMP CAMPAIGN INSIDER REVEALS STRATEGY BEHIND MIDTERM BLITZ THAT WHITE HOUSE HOPES PAYS OFF BIG
"Please pretend I'm on the freaking ballot," Trump urged. "And in a really, in a certain way, I am on the ballot because they can take away everything that we, that we got."
The president took Blakeman's challenge to Democrat Gov. Kathy Hochul as the centerpiece of the rally, promising direct support from Washington if elected.
"[Blakeman will] save this state. He'll turn the state around and I'll help him from the White House ," Trump said. "I'll be helping him for governor."

Trump blasted Hochul over New York 's taxes, utility bills and public safety, arguing that Blakeman could unleash the state's economic potential by embracing domestic energy production and cutting costs for families.
DEBRA MESSING SAYS COST OF LIVING, SUBWAY VIOLENCE PUSHED HER TO BACK TRUMP-ENDORSED REPUBLICAN
The president also hailed his administration's economic agenda as proof of what Trump described as a remarkable national turnaround.

He singled out Micron's planned $100 billion semiconductor complex in central New York, a project the company says is expected to generate 50,000 jobs across the state, including 9,000 directly with Micron.
"This will soon be the home to the largest semiconductor manufacturing facility ever built in the Western Hemisphere," Trump said.

Blakeman joined Trump onstage and echoed the president's message of a Republican resurgence, promising to cut taxes and utility bills, focus on public safety and make New York more attractive to both businesses and families.
"We have to create good jobs, good benefits to keep our young people here," Blakeman said. "We gotta look at business not as the enemy, but as a partner."

Trump also threw his support behind Republican congressional candidates Kailee Buller, who is challenging Democrat Rep. John Mannion in New York's 22nd District, and Anthony Constantino , who is running for the state's open 21st District seat, pledging to help Republicans compete for both seats.
The rally also notably featured a brief but memorable on-stage appearance by legendary former heavyweight boxing champion Mike Tyson, whom Trump invited up before the crowd.

"I'm just happy to be up here with my president, President Trump," Tyson said. "And, there's no way in the world I would ever be here if it wasn't for a president like Donald Trump. Thank you. Thank you very much."
Trump responded with a laugh, recalling Tyson's notorious reputation.
"I don't want to fight him," Trump joked, before complimenting the former champion. "You look good. Mike. What the h— are you doing?"
With Election Day approaching , the president returned to his core message that Republicans need Trump supporters to make a roaring showing at the ballot box.
"We're going to elect a Republican House and Republican Senate," Trump said.

articles.headline: Trump fumes over Nobel peace prize snub and criticizes Norway
keyFacts: Donald Trump criticized Norway and the Nobel committee after not receiving the 2026 Nobel peace prize.
The prize was awarded to Navi Pillay, a former United Nations human rights official.
Trump claimed he will quickly settle or win the ongoing conflicts involving Iran and Russia-Ukraine.
body: Donald Trump complained Friday about not winning the Nobel peace prize for 2026, a year in which he started a war with Iran.
At what was supposed to be a rally for other Republican candidates in Syracuse, New York, the US president devoted a long portion of his speech airing his grievances with the Nobel committee.

“The United States of America, represented by me as your president, should have received the Nobel peace prize, but didn’t. And this is an indelible stain on the country of Norway, and those people that made such a disgraceful and embarrassing decision,” Trump said.

“The Nobel peace prize has been forever discredited by a handful of radical ideologues who are anti-democracy and really enemies of civilization,” Trump went on. “We will not forget, Norway, that you didn’t give this prize.”

Trump also recited a list of wars he claims to have settled, some of which were not wars and some that are still not settled, before adding: “I’m about to settle or win two more: Iran and Russia-Ukraine.”
Trump said he would be ending both wars “quickly”.
“I will tell you what,” he added, darkly. “Iran will be very quick one way or the other: that they give us everything or they don’t exist any longer.”

“Additionally, I stopped Iran from having a nuclear weapon and blowing up the entire Middle East and ultimately far beyond the Middle East, including Europe, perhaps the US and I saved more lives than anyone in history,” Trump claimed, despite the fact that US intelligence agencies reported to Congress in 2025 that Iran had actually suspended its pursuit of nuclear weapons in 2003.

“Despite all of this and all of these unbelievable accomplishments, the Nobel prize was given out today to a liberal person who works at the United Nations, who nobody has ever heard of,” Trump said of Navi Pillay, the South African former UN human rights chief who chaired the UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza.

articles.headline: Magic: The Gathering Returns to Marvel with Darkhold Destiny
keyFacts: Wizards of the Coast and Marvel are releasing a third crossover set titled Darkhold Destiny, featuring an original in-house story where Dormammu and Hela invade the multiverse.
The set focuses heavily on spellcasting divided into Arcane, Divine, and Dark schools of magic, and includes products such as booster packs, commander decks, and scene boxes.
Wizards of the Coast will preview the original Marvel story with an Image comics publication in February, leading up to the set's launch in April 2027.
body: Magic: The Gathering and Marvel have already crossed over a couple of times with Spider-Man and the Marvel Super Heroes set last year. But for its third Marvel set, MTG is getting spooky with Darkhold Destiny.

Rather than being based in a fairly mundane version of New York, Darkhold Destiny is taking the likes of Doctor Strange and the Asgardians and telling a more magical story (forgive me). What really separates this new out-there set from the other two Marvel sets is that Wizards of the Coast was really able to write its own story with Marvel's characters and settings, which makes them feel less like a crossover and more like a part of Magic's multiverse.

With a new story written in-house, Wizards of the Coast was also able to give its artists more license to create their own takes on Marvel characters. For instance, with Scarlet Witch in the Marvel Super Heroes set, she looks like a pretty standard take on her comic book appearance. But in the art I was shown for Darkhold Destiny, she looks much more like an MTG character, while still retaining some of the signature parts of her outfit – the mask is still there.

I was also given broad strokes of what the story is about. Essentially, Dormammu and Hela use the Darkhold to invade the entire multiverse, and it's up to Doctor Strange, Thor, and other Marvel heroes to stop them. Of course, because of the characters and, well, props that the story revolves around, the set is focused heavily on spellcasting.

Thematically, the spellcasting is focused on what's essentially three different 'schools' of magic: Arcane, Divine, and Dark. Arcane magic will be themed around Doctor Strange and his allies, while Divine magic will be wielded by the Asgardians and other similar... entities. Dark magic is primarily going to be wielded by the villains of the set, but there are some heroes, like Ghost Rider that will apparently be wielding Dark magic.

You can expect a lot of focus on cool instants, sorceries and 'unique enchantments.' Wizards is even bringing back the Arcane subtype on instants and sorceries, which hasn't been used since Saviors of Kamigawa all the way back in 2005. I even asked if WotC is bringing back the obscure 'Splice Onto Arcane' ability that let you combine different arcane spells, but sadly, it is not.

Just like any other recent set, there will be a whole lineup of different Darkhold Destiny products. The standard fare is all here, Booster Packs, Collector Boosters and Bundles; but there will also be four commander decks.
- Strange Academy (White/Blue/Black)
- Gods of Asgard (White/Red/Green)
- Midnight Sons (White/Black)
- Lords of Hel (Black/Red)

Each of these commander decks will also have a collector's edition available, which will be completely decked out in foils. There will also be two scene boxes, each with six mechanically unique cards. Both the Bundle and the special Gift Bundle will also come with a mechanically unique promo card, and I just hope they don't skyrocket immediately on TCGPlayer, but I know that they probably will.

Wizards of the Coast will be giving the first glimpse of its original Marvel story in February with a comic produced alongside Image comics. Then, another comic will come out closer to when the set launches in April 2027.

articles.headline: Marvel Darkhold Destiny Is Magic: The Gathering’s First Universes Beyond Set Of 2027
keyFacts: Wizards of the Coast announced Marvel Darkhold Destiny as Magic: The Gathering’s first Universes Beyond set of 2027 during New York Comic Con.
The April 9 release features normal and Collector booster packs, four commander decks, and introduces a brand-new character in a February Marvel Infinity comic.
The set features an original co-created story, gameplay mechanics like Vengeance, and the return of the Arcane subtype.
body: Today at New York Comic Con, Wizards of the Coast announced the first 2027 Universes Beyond expansion set for Magic: The Gathering. Marvel’s Darkhold Destiny will pit Doctor Strange, Thor, Ghost Rider, and more against cosmic villains like Hela and Dormammu in 2027.

The set will include normal and Collector booster packs, and four pre-constructed commander decks themed around Marvel heroes and villains, including the Midnight Sons. Multiple cards were shown during the hour-long panel, including Magic, who transforms into Darkchild, Gargantos, and the titular Darkhold.

Darkhold Destiny tells an original story co-created by designers at Marvel and Wizards of the Coast. Along with that story, a brand-new character created for this set will be introduced in a Marvel Infinity comic series starting in February.

Mechanics include Vengeance, an Adventure-like gameplay feature that lets you cast spells from your graveyard and return the permanent it's attached to back to the battlefield, and the return of the Arcane subtype for spells.
Darkhold Destiny launches April 9 in big-box retailers and local game stores.

articles.headline: 2026's OLED monitors can nearly recreate the sublime clarity of a '90s CRT, but Windows will have to change before we can achieve true nirvana
keyFacts: Developers Mark Rejhon and Timothy Lottes created an algorithm that simulates the motion clarity and phosphor fade of a 1990s CRT monitor on modern displays.
App developer Mausimus built a tool called ShaderBeam to apply this CRT simulation, though it requires complex setups and struggles against Windows and GPU scheduling limits.
Mausimus and Rejhon stated that true mainstream adoption requires operating system builders, GPU makers, and display manufacturers to natively support the technology in the future.
body: The 2007 season finale of TV phenom Lost ended with an all-timer twist: What had seemed like the show's routine flashback storyline, filling in the events that preceded its characters ending up in island purgatory, was actually a flash forward. Protagonists Jack and Kate were somehow safe in Los Angeles after three seasons of being stuck on the mysterious island. Escaping had been the whole point of the show—or so we thought, until a broken Jack cried "We have to go back!"

This is now how I feel about, frankly, a lot of technology. Not long before that episode aired I'd gleefully dropped $1,000 on my first HD display, a 26-inch 1366x768 Samsung LCD that served as my college dorm TV and doubled as my computer monitor. For the time it was state of the art, so much thinner and sharper and better than the CRT monitor still attached to the family PC.
Or was it?
Twenty years later, experts who are tuned into the minutia of display tech are still trying to get back what we lost.

"People older than 40 will generally remember the motion clarity of CRTs, while younger people who've never seen a CRT will not remember," says Mark Rejhon, founder of the website Blur Busters. For years, Blur Busters' "Test UFO" browser tool, starring a little green man in a red saucer, has served as the de facto way to judge the clarity of objects in motion on modern displays. Compared to older CRT monitors, the LCDs of the mid-2000s were particularly terrible, their pixels taking an eternity to change from one color to another and leaving a nasty "ghost" trail on fast-moving images.

The TV I spent an entire month's paycheck on was better than average for its day, but the novelty of the HD era made me overlook then what's far more obvious now: the richer colors and smoothness of a CRT that I gave up, and wouldn't get back for nearly two decades.
Today's high refresh monitors are far better than the smeary, washed out LCDs of the 2000s—but even the best of the best are still chasing the clarity of CRTs, which means Rejhon is chasing it too.
The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products
Cathode ray 'tude

While ShaderBeam tries to eradicate motion blur in software, Nvidia's tackling it in hardware. G-Sync Pulsar (built into a range of gaming monitors this year) works with VRR and uses backlight strobing plus a rolling top-to-bottom refresh cycle, much like a CRT, to create a "perceived clarity" of 1,000 Hz. No OLEDs yet, though, and the tech is of course locked to Nvidia GPUs.

In late 2024 Rejhon debuted a "breakthrough algorithm for simulating a CRT tube" alongside former Nvidia developer Timothy Lottes, which takes advantage of 240+ Hz displays to drastically reduce visible motion blur in retro games and other content that's locked at 60 Hz.

The trick, to grossly simplify some extremely complicated tech, is recreating the visual "phosphor fade" of a CRT, which is gentler on the eyes and less flickery than harsh black frame insertion (BFI), the previous go-to method for cutting down on blur as pixels swap from one color to another.

"The two main ways to reduce display motion blur is either flicker the frames (like a CRT) or add more frame rate (for high Hz)," Rejhon said. "Both methods will show frames more briefly, like a fast camera shutter, and result in less display motion blur. CRTs could flicker pixels brightly for less than 1/1000 second. The bonus with CRT is you do not require more frame rate to achieve low motion blur."

If that's still tough to wrap your brain around, think of the CRT simulation as DLSS, but for motion instead of resolution: When it's working just right, a game locked at 60 frames per second could look just as smooth and clean as one running at, say, 540 frames per second, without needing an RTX 5090 to hit those numbers.

540 Hz is the refresh rate of the ROG PG27AQWP-W Asus sent me for testing, an ideal monitor for getting the most out of CRT simulation. It even has a 720 Hz mode if you drop the resolution to 720p; and the higher the refresh, the more you can reduce the perceived motion blur. Unlike LCDs, OLED panels can go completely black (there's no backlight to bleed light) and get extremely bright, getting much closer to the contrast CRTs naturally offered. And the high refresh rate helps recreate the electron beam that would travel down a CRT screen to "draw" the image.

This effect isn't just a nostalgia thing: As Rejhon notes on BlurBusters, "60 Hz BFI and strobing flickers a lot" because you're flashing a black frame in between each one from your game. By comparison, the top-to-bottom scanning effect is less harsh: "CRT simulation is much gentler for 60 fps content, because of phosphor fade & rolling scan. Some light is emitted somewhere else on the screen all the time."
Despite the perfect hardware to test on, though, CRT simulation is so bleeding edge I practically sliced my brain to ribbons trying to get it working earlier this year.

The first actual implementation of BlurBusters' tech was in a shader for the emulation frontend Retroarch, but soon after it was built into an experimental branch of a standalone app called ShaderGlass, a great overlay for Windows that lets you apply hundreds of visual effects to whatever's on your desktop—scanlines, the fuzziness of an analog video signal, and so on. But the CRT beam simulation is so much more complex than a typical video shader, app developer Mausimus decided to split it off into a separate tool: ShaderBeam.

"The ideal application of beam simulation technology requires perfect synchronization with both the display (it cannot afford to drop a single frame even at those high refresh rates, since that causes very noticeable flashing) and input content (for aligning source frame generation with simulated CRT refresh rate)," said Mausimus. Right now, it's the best way to use Rejhon's algorithm.
Shader dreams

ShaderBeam doesn't involve much setup: launch its executable and use a hotkey to apply the shader on top of a game window. How simple it looks belies how hard the visual effect is to pull off when you don't work at Microsoft, AMD or Nvidia.

"ShaderBeam tries to use whatever's available, like screen capture and window transparency (even though these technologies weren't designed with this use case in mind at all and provide no timing guarantees whatsoever), to compensate for the inability to insert itself into the rendering pipeline from source content to display," Mausimus said. "It's at the mercy of opaque scheduling algorithms built into the OS and GPU drivers, hoping it can eke out enough resources to maintain its timing."

The ideal ShaderBeam setup involves disabling usual niceties like VRR, turning off all sorts of features in your graphic's cards driver settings, unplugging secondary monitors, using Process Lasso to give it higher priority, and even a registry edit. It includes the novel idea of splitting up the responsibilities of rendering the game and the CRT shader to two GPUs. If your processor has a built-in GPU, using it can help avoid a desync between the rate at which your game is spitting out frames and the rate at which ShaderBeam can apply the CRT beam simulation.

"By moving beam simulation to another GPU there is less contention for the primary GPU's time and effectively better scheduling consistency; it does provide a much more stable experience," Mausimus said. "The issue with single GPU isn't lack of GPU power, rather its unpredictable distribution."

If ShaderBeam "isn't given enough GPU time by the OS to present a frame on time," you'll experience some flashing—which I discovered by pushing my Intel chip's iGPU to output at 1440p at 540 Hz. Then I struggled through consistent stuttering while trying ShaderBeam with various emulators and shooters like Quake and Amid Evil, which led me down the rabbit hole of display subframe timing, where the minutia of monitor technology quickly becomes more and more arcane.

This all might sound like a borderline deranged amount of effort just to play a game like Nintendo's Metroid Prime 2: Echoes in GameCube emulator Dolphin, one of my test cases, the way I first saw it on the CRT in a high school friend's bedroom. I felt like a mad scientist (emphasis on the mad) while trying to troubleshoot stutters, flicker, and color banding for hours on end.

Even when everything is calibrated just right, there's also the possibility a game itself can throw a wrench in things—Unreal Engine 5's penchant for stuttering will naturally throw off the frame pacing of the CRT simulation, too, for example.

But when I started rolling Samus's morph ball in a tight circle and realized the room's columns remained pin sharp even as the camera whirled around, I got a glimpse of what Rejhon and Mausimus have been fighting for. "On moving objects (or the scene if you look around) the shader should allow you to see the individual pixels; normally they all just get blurred out," Mausimus said, using the intricate textures on a Quake column as a prime example. Factorio is another good test case: "It has this really smooth movement of the whole scene when you walk around without the shader, the pixels get blurred together, but with the shader you should still be able to see the details even when moving."
Hard Locked
On top of a vast library of 60 Hz console games, these PC classics would benefit from CRT simulation.
Dark Souls: Remastered
It took until Armored Core 6 for FromSoftware to offer 120 fps support.
Sonic Racing: Crossworlds
A 2025 racing game capped at 60 fps? No speeding tickets for Sonic, I guess.
Nier: Automata
An action game this good begs for an uncapped framerate. Alas.
Mirror's Edge
Tweaks exist to uncap Mirror's Edge, but the physics get wonky. Its gleaming cityscape deserves the clarity of a CRT.

It almost feels uncanny once your eyes pick up on details that would normally be just a blur—the difference is as dramatic as switching to a higher refresh rate in a game you've only ever controlled at 30 fps. But it's frustratingly difficult to describe or demonstrate, since capturing the effect on camera is tough and impossible to perceive without a 240 Hz+ display, anyway.
Future vision

As impressive as ShaderBeam is, it ultimately requires a level of fiddling and compromise that I don't think make sense for anyone right now. It intermittently brings back what we left behind when we abandoned CRTs, but ultimately makes me think the real solution is either going to come from new hardware—like the next generation of Nvidia's Pulsar monitors—or from Microsoft digging into the guts of Windows to change some of the stuff that happens in between .exe and screen.

"Even if ShaderBeam's makeshift workarounds never reach levels of consistency needed for wide adoption, the hope is that they will boost users' interest in having this kind of technology properly supported by OS, GPU and display manufacturers," Mausimus said.
Rejhon seems bullish about that eventually coming to pass… but these things take time.

"In the future, when shader hooks are built into operating systems, as well as video-processing GPUs are integrated into the display of the 2030s, it will be much more user friendly," he predicted. "This is part of the advocacy that is being encouraged by Blur Busters' Open Source Display Shaders Initiative."

ShaderBeam's goal of awakening PC gamers to the benefits of CRT simulation worked on me, at least. I'm convinced we have to go back—even if it means dragging the people in charge of graphics drivers back to CRT paradise with us.
Why you should consider a CRT for your PC gaming setup this year
Despite their bulk, the vivid colors and low latency of a CRT can still make the right PC games look absolutely incredible today.

Wes has been covering games and hardware for more than 10 years, first at tech sites like The Wirecutter and Tested before joining the PC Gamer team in 2014. Wes plays a little bit of everything, but he'll always jump at the chance to cover emulation and Japanese games.

When he's not obsessively optimizing and re-optimizing a tangle of conveyor belts in Satisfactory (it's really becoming a problem), he's probably playing a 20-year-old Final Fantasy or some opaque ASCII roguelike. With a focus on writing and editing features, he seeks out personal stories and in-depth histories from the corners of PC gaming and its niche communities. 50% pizza by volume (deep dish, to be specific).

articles.headline: Move Over ‘Carrie’: Mike Flanagan Teases His ‘Exorcist’ Movie at NYCC 2026
keyFacts: Director Mike Flanagan promoted his film The Exorcist: Martyrs at New York Comic Con, calling it the scariest movie he has made.
The movie stars Scarlett Johansson as an NYPD detective tracking a serial killer played by John Leguizamo.
The Exorcist: Martyrs premieres in theaters on Friday, March 12, 2027.
body: Mike Flanagan is a busy man. Just this week, his TV series remake of Stephen King‘s horror classic, Carrie, premiered on Prime Video. Clayface, the body-horror movie inspired by the DC Comics character, for which he cowrote the script, hits theaters on Oct. 23.
Now, he’s onto promoting his next completed project, The Exorcist: Martyrs, a film he called “the scariest movie I’ve ever made,” while at Friday’s Blumhouse panel at New York Comic Con.

If you’ve been keeping track, Flanagan’s name has been attached to the iconic horror franchise, which began in 1973 and is based on the William Peter Blatty novel of the same name. Since Linda Blair terrified audiences as the demon-possessed young girl, Regan MacNeil, the movie series expanded. There have been sequels, a prequel and even a short-lived TV show.
More from CNET
In 2023, David Gordon Green attempted to reboot the franchise with The Exorcist: The Believer. Now, it’s Flanagan’s turn.

The Exorcist: Martyrs gives a new spin on the Exorcist canon and injects a Minderhunter-style serial killer narrative element into the mix. If you watched the TV series I mentioned above, you’ll notice a similar procedural vibe in the brand-new trailer that dropped during the panel. And if you’re an Exorcist III stan, I’m sure you’ll be happy with the just released clip, as it’s got that similar brooding feeling here.

The Exorcist: Martyrs stars Scarlett Johansson as an NYPD detective tracking a serial killer named Father Sunday (John Leguizamo), who uses Catholic iconography in his kills. Chiwetel Ejiofor, fresh out of The Backrooms, also stars in the film, opposite Laurence Fishburne, Sasha Calle and Jacobi Jupe.

If you’ve been yearning for the Mike Flanagan era of Oculus and The Haunting of Hill House, The Exorcist: Martyrs feels like the filmmaker is back in his terrifying groove. While I’m still waiting for his adaptation of Stephen King’s The Dark Tower to see the light of day, this will have to do.
The Exorcist: Martyrs premieres in theaters on Friday, March 12, 2027.

articles.headline: The Trump administration plans a public killing
keyFacts: The Pentagon announced plans to publicly execute and livestream the death of former Army major Nidal Hasan via firing squad.
Hasan was sentenced to death for a 2009 mass shooting at Fort Hood that killed 13 people and wounded over 30.
The execution is scheduled for December 3, but Hasan's legal team could potentially delay it through federal court challenges.
body: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth speaks from a stage in Sparrows Point, Maryland, on October 6, 2026. | Win McNamee/Getty Images
This story appeared in The Logoff , a daily newsletter that helps you stay informed about the Trump administration without letting political news take over your life. Subscribe here .
Welcome to The Logoff: The Trump administration is planning a public killing.

What’s happening? On Thursday, the Pentagon announced that it would execute Nidal Hasan, a former Army major sentenced to death for a 2009 mass shooting on a military base, publicly and on livestream.

The execution, if it happens, would be unprecedented: The last widely reported public execution in the US was 90 years ago , in Kentucky, but to stream a death live would be something else entirely. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has promoted the announcement with something approaching glee, telling a reporter that “we’ll make sure that people are able to watch it.”
What’s the context? According to the Pentagon, Hasan will be executed via firing squad on December 3 — the first such execution by the military in more than 80 years.

Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist, was sentenced to death in 2013 by a military jury following a court-martial for the 2009 shooting, when he killed 13 people and wounded more than 30 at Fort Hood in Texas. The execution is set to be carried out at the same Army post.

Will the Pentagon go through with this? It’s unclear, for multiple reasons. The Pentagon’s announcement that Hasan’s death will be livestreamed has generated a great deal of bipartisan pushback, as well as condemnation by religious groups , though that is unlikely to stop the execution itself.

The head of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops decried the decision to livestream the execution as “a barbaric promotion of a culture of death,” and retiring Sen. Thom Tillis (R-NC) called it the decision “beyond disgusting.”
“Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do,” Tillis wrote in a post on X.
On Friday, Vice President JD Vance also said that he was unsure if the livestream would take place .
Hasan’s legal team could also delay the execution substantially — potentially for multiple years — by challenging his detention in federal court, though he has exhausted the military appeals process.
And with that, it’s time to log off…

articles.headline: Neanderthal wooden tools from Spain found preserved in stone
keyFacts: Spanish archaeologists cataloged 597 Neanderthal wooden tool impressions preserved in stone at the Abric Romaní rock shelter.
The preserved artifacts include spears, digging sticks, bark trays, shelter components, and a novel wooden club.
Archaeologist M. Gema Chacón said the discoveries show Neanderthals routinely engaged in woodworking for varied subsistence tasks beyond hunting.
body: The Stone Age owes its name to tools that survived to our time. The material early humans worked with most, though, was probably wood because it is so much easier to process. Unfortunately, we know very little about Paleolithic woodwork because wood rots relatively quickly. But at Abric Romaní, a rock shelter in Capellades, west of Barcelona, mineral-rich water coated wooden Neanderthal tools in a limestone-like crust. When wood rotted away, it left behind hollow molds that faithfully reflect its shape.

In a recent Science Advances study, a team of Spanish archaeologists has cataloged 597 wooden remains from Neanderthal living areas dating from 62,000 to 40,000 years ago. They found spears, digging sticks, bark trays, parts of shelters, and a club unlike anything seen before, suggesting Neanderthals were likely much more than just Homo sapiens’ dumber cousins.
Beyond hunting gear

The oldest wooden artifacts we have are mostly weapons. They include spears from a German town called Schöningen, a spear tip from Clacton-on-Sea in England, and the spear found alongside an elephant skeleton in Lehringen, Germany. Most came from waterlogged sediments, where a lack of oxygen slowed decay.

The spears mostly give us information about how Neanderthals hunted. The findings at Abric Romaní are different because the finds come from a place where Neanderthals lived, slept, cooked, and made tools over the course of some 20,000 years.

“We have a sample of wooden tools for different subsistence activities, not only hunting,” says M. Gema Chacón, an archaeologist at the Catalan Institute of Human Paleoecology and Social Evolution (IPHES-CERCA) and co-author of the study. Because wood turns up in level after level, it shows that woodworking was routine for Neanderthals rather than an occasional one-off.

Google plans to officially reveal the new wearable on October 12.
body: Google teases its new 'Fitbit Edge' wearable ahead of an October 12 reveal
The company has essentially confirmed it's releasing another fitness tracker.

Previous leaked images revealed the name and design of Google's rumored "Fitbit Edge" fitness tracker and now the company has essentially confirmed both in new posts on Instagram and X. The wearable is rumored to fit between the screenless Fitbit Air Google launched earlier this year and the more premium Pixel Watch 5.

Google's posts include an image of what appears to be a side button on the new wearable, and the following caption: "Get an Edge on your health. 10.12.26." The choice to capitalize "Edge" seems to confirm the name of the wearable, and October 12 is likely the day Google plans to reveal it.
Get an Edge on your health. 10.12.26 pic.twitter.com/1zRU0eoAS7
— Google Health (@googlehealth) October 9, 2026

Images of this new Fitbit device have been kicking around since at least August, when 9to5Google spotted an unnamed fitness tracker in some of Google's Pixel 11 marketing. But the name of the wearable wasn't revealed until Android Headlines shared images of the Fitbit Edge and details of its built-in apps and health tracking features earlier this week. Those details were further fleshed out in a report from French magazine Dealabs, which confirmed the device's design and name, and included additional information on its battery life and possible price. The Edge will reportedly last for up to seven days on a charge if its always-on display is disabled, and two days if it's on, and could cost €179 (about $200) when it goes on sale in Europe. But considering the Fitbit Air starts at $99 in the US and €99 in Europe, the new tracker could wind up being closer to $180 in the US.

The last similarly-sized fitness tracker Google introduced was the Fitbit Charge 6 in 2023, so the company is due for a new release. If it's everything reporting has described it to be, the Fitbit Edge seems like a natural step up from the Fitbit Air, and another way to push people to a Google Health Premium subscription. We'll just have to wait until October 12 to see if Google follows through.

articles.headline: ‘Beyond Disgusting’: The Right Wing Is At Odds Over Hegseth’s Public Execution Plan
keyFacts: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced plans to livestream the firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan.
The plan drew criticism from several Republican and Democratic lawmakers, while some right-wing commentators defended it.
Hegseth said the execution is scheduled for Dec. 3, with a Pentagon official confirming that livestream details will follow.
body: Some elected Republicans are bristling at a shocking claim from Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth that the Trump administration plans to livestream the firing squad execution of the infamous Fort Hood shooter, with one lawmaker calling the plan “beyond disgusting.”

But the reaction from influential figures on the right has been wildly different, with some celebrating public executions as “healthy” expression and framing anyone opposing the Pentagon plan as a hypocritical leftist or a terrorist sympathizer.

Hegseth on Thursday excitedly shared his plan to publicly execute former Army Maj. Nidal Malik Hasan, whose death by firing squad President Donald Trump approved this week after he killed 13 people in a mass shooting at Fort Hood, Texas, in 2009. Aboard the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln, the defense secretary told right-wing commentator and political operative Jack Posobiec the Pentagon would “make sure that people are able to watch” Hasan’s execution by firing squad.
“[P]eople need to understand that there’s serious consequences for these types of things,” Hegseth said.

Posobiec, promoting his interview with the Pentagon chief, has vigorously defended the plan to publicly execute Hasan. In a flurry of social media posts Thursday and Friday, the right-winger and Real America’s Voice television host argued livestreaming the execution was not “bloodlust” but rather a “display of justice” that was “biblical and moral.”
And Posobiec painted opposition to Hasan’s public killing as primarily liberal outrage.
“The Left only cares about Hasan [because] he is a terrorist,” he wrote in one post. “None of these people would have a problem with a public execution if it was a White guy,” he followed up.
But critics of the Pentagon’s plan to livestream a state execution were not confined to the left.

“Hasan should face the death penalty, but making his execution public and streaming it? Beyond disgusting,” said Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) on Thursday night. “Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do. It should not be happening in America.”

Conservative radio host Erick Erickson argued the execution would be easy fodder for anti-American sentiment abroad. “One thing is for sure, in the Middle East, they’ll be passing out .mp4 files of the Nidal Hassan [sic] execution to celebrate his martyrdom and recruit new terrorists,” he wrote in a post on X.
Tillis and Erickson were joined in opposition Friday by Rep. Austin Scott (R-Ga.), who said he supported the death sentence for Hasan but that “live-streaming executions is what jihadists do.”
“America is better than that,” Scott added.

And GOP Sen. John Curtis (R-Utah), who’s become increasingly willing to break with the Trump administration, invoked Roman philosopher Seneca, who he said in a social media post warned that the “bloody spectacles” of the ancient empire “corrupted” those who watched them.

“A civilization erodes when it cultivates an appetite for executions as a form of entertainment,” wrote Curtis. “Secretary Hegseth’s plan to livestream the Fort Hood execution risks feeding that appetite.”

The Utah Republican continued that while he thought the victims of Hasan’s crimes deserved justice, Hegseth’s plan to broadcast his execution was not an “effective deterrent” for future acts of terror. “I urge him to reconsider,” Curtis said.

The reservations of establishment Republicans, though, were far from the majority view — GOP lawmakers remained largely silent on the matter. And their skepticism was less than convincing for MAGA influencers and right-wing thought leaders.
“The hysterical crashout you are seeing over this from many supposed ‘conservatives’ shows you who is not prepared to do what it takes to save Western civilization,” retorted Posobiec.

Charles Cornish-Dale, a British far-right commentator who goes by the online handle “Raw Egg Nationalist,” pointed to a post from Erickson made during the Jan. 6, 2021, Capitol riot in which the radio host suggested law enforcement shoot rioters.

“This dude who was calling to shoot ordinary Americans who had the courage to protest a stolen election suddenly has a fit of conscience when the person being shot is an actual enemy of America who killed 13 American soldiers,” wrote Cornish-Dale.

Right-wingers have also defended plans to publicly execute Hasan by claiming the U.S. has a long history of such events. Posobiec and others pointed out that George Washington oversaw public executions. And New Hampshire Libertarian Party chairman Jeremy Kauffman cited the 1936 killing of Rainey Bethea, the last person publicly executed in the U.S.
Kauffman quoted a Time Magazine article from the time which described “tipsy merrymakers” and “hanging parties” in Owensboro, Kentucky, the night before Bethea’s public hanging.
“It is healthy to celebrate the elimination of evil,” the libertarian political leader wrote.

Democrats were broadly aghast at the Pentagon’s plan to kill Hasan in public and on camera. Sen. Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.), a veteran, said public executions were “the kind of thing Iran and the Taliban do” and called on Hegseth to be removed from office “immediately.”

“Public executions have no place in a democracy,” said Sen. Dick Durbin (D-Ill.), the top Democrat on the Senate Judiciary Committee. “We as a nation cannot stoop to the level of the people we seek to punish.”

Hegseth, meanwhile, said Thursday the execution would take place at Fort Hood on Dec. 3 at one o’clock in the afternoon — the time Hasan began his shooting. A Pentagon official confirmed to HuffPost the execution “will be livestreamed” but declined to say where or how. “Details will follow,” the official said.

It’s unclear whether Hasan’s execution would be allowed on any major social media platform or streaming service, most of which bar violent or graphic content. Representatives for Meta, Google and X did not return requests for comment on whether their services would carry the execution.

A spokesperson for TikTok, where the White House posts to more than 7 million followers, did not directly address the issue but pointed HuffPost to its policy that bans “depictions of real-world graphic incidents and violence, such as torture, the moment of someone’s death or the shooting of an individual.”
Even with Hegseth’s confident bluster, though, it appears even some in the Trump administration are uncomfortable with streaming a public execution.
Vice President JD Vance on Friday poured cold water on the whole plan, adding that even if the Pentagon followed through on its proposal to kill Hasan on camera, he wouldn’t be tuning in.
“I don’t know that that’s actually going to happen,” Vance told reporters. “If it’s all through live stream, I’m not going to be watching it.”

articles.headline: Tottenham happy to be called name again after previous request to the media
keyFacts: Tottenham Hotspur is reincorporating 'Tottenham' into its club branding two years after asking media to avoid using the standalone name.
The club previously instructed media in a brand playbook to never refer to them simply as 'Tottenham'.
Tottenham sits bottom of the Premier League table with two points ahead of their upcoming match against Manchester United.
body: Tottenham have backtracked on their omission of ‘Tottenham’ from club branding – two years after requesting alternative names.
The north London club launched a new ‘brand identity’ in November 2024 that featured changes to their logo and signature font.
Spurs look as though they are heading back to being simply named as ‘Tottenham’ despite a past media request Getty
It was later revealed that they wrote to broadcasters asking for them to be referred to as either ‘Tottenham Hotspur’ or ‘Spurs’.
‘Tottenham’ was seemingly brushed aside but, as per The Athletic, it could be on its way back .
Fans attending home matches are said to have seen signs that read ‘This is Tottenham ‘ upon arrival.
They also launched a short film during the summer called ‘Tottenham ‘Til I Die’, with ‘Hotspur’ being dropped once again.
At the time of writing, the Premier League still call them ‘Tottenham Hotspur’ on their website, although this could change soon.
What did Tottenham want to be called?
The reintegration of ‘Tottenham’ comes after the new brand identity included a club request for what they wanted to be named as.
“When referring to the team or the brand, please use ‘Tottenham Hotspur’, ‘Tottenham Hotspur Football Club’ or ‘THFC’,” said a ‘Brand Playbook’.
It addd: “Never refer to our Club as ‘Tottenham’, ‘Tottenham Hotspur FC’ or ‘TH’.”
Founded in 1882, they were originally named ‘Hotspur Football Club’ and based in Northumberland Park, which is in north Tottenham.
‘Tottenham Hotspur Football Club’ became their official name two years later.
‘Tottenham Hotspur’ was the preferred name used by the club, although it looks as though it will be toned down Getty
Spurs are back!
After the three-week international break, Spurs return to Premier League action this weekend.
They travel to Manchester United on Saturday evening in search of their first win of the season.
Spurs lost 3-0 at Brentford on the opening weekend before falling to a 2-0 home defeat against Newcastle United.
Back-to-back 0-0 draws with Nottingham Forest and Everton were then followed by a 3-2 loss to Aston Villa.
The results mean they sit bottom of the Premier League table with two points gained from a possible 15.
As things stand, Spurs could be battling against relegation to the Championship yet again.

articles.headline: Decade-old RAM is making a comeback
keyFacts: Intel and AMD are producing new CPUs that support older DDR4 memory to address rising DDR5 RAM prices.
Gigabyte announced new motherboards for AMD's older AM4 platform alongside the relaunch of a Ryzen CPU.
New Intel chips compatible with DDR4 RAM are expected to launch in early 2027, according to Gigabyte.
body: CPU makers have noticed that the seemingly unending RAM price hikes are making it tough for a lot of us to upgrade our PCs. Their solution? A return to last-gen DDR4 RAM. Intel and AMD are making new CPUs that’ll support the older, more affordable type of memory.
Decade-old RAM is making a comeback
The RAM shortage is bringing back DDR4, with new Intel and AMD CPUs for older RAM, sockets, and chipsets.

On Friday, Gigabyte announced that two of its motherboard lines will support “upcoming” processors built on Intel’s LGA 1700 socket. That socket debuted in 2021 with the 12th gen Alder Lake CPUs and supported both DDR4 RAM and the then-new DDR5 RAM. Intel dropped it for a DDR5-only approach in 2024. But according to Gigabyte, the dual format support is now being revived, with new LGA 1700 chips “expected to launch in early 2027.”
Intel did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

This backtrack stems from LGA 1700’s cross-compatibility with both kinds of RAM — an advantage over its successor that’s recently become much more important. Intel’s strategy may be to offer users the choice of a new CPU that doesn’t require them to switch to new, and very expensive, DDR5 memory, too. AMD is doing something similar: in August, Gigabyte also announced a new series of motherboards for AMD’s last-gen, DDR4-compatible AM4 platform to go along with the 10th-anniversary relaunch of the Ryzen 7 5800X3D CPU.

DDR4 started hitting the market in 2014 and has since been succeeded by the much faster DDR5. Under normal circumstances, buying new hardware to use technology that’s over a decade old would probably be a bad investment. But the RAM shortage is changing the math, with DDR4 RAM seemingly feeling the sting of price hikes much less than DDR5.

I recently saw the price disparity first-hand while shopping around for new RAM after a DDR4 kit abruptly died on me. Right now, a DDR5 32GB Corsair Vengeance RAM kit costs $620, while the corresponding DDR4 kit costs $260. Even though it’s more than 32GB of DDR4 RAM typically cost back in mid-2025, that’s more than double the price for DDR5! Of course, DDR5 has significant advantages, like higher speeds and better power efficiency. But those perks might not be worth the current price of admission.

It could be years before prices drop again, a reality that’s starting to really sink in with the official return of older sockets and chipsets. But at least it’s a good time to hang onto your DDR4 RAM.

articles.headline: We Might Be Cooked, As These Vibe-Coded Web Browser Ports Of Halo, The Simpsons: Hit And Run, And GTA: Vice City Seem To Work Perfectly

body: In the past couple of weeks, hundreds of vibe-coded, AI-decompiled emulators and games have appeared out of thin air. Why? Because Claudeâs latest update, Claude Opus 5.5, is extremely good at decompiling.

The short of it is that a gameâs source code can now be compiled and reconstructed in record timeâsomething that used to take coders months to achieve. All of those ânativeâ Fallout and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare ports and those AI-generated Super Mario 64 inside Elden Ring mash-up mods you may have seen are a direct result of this.

However, I think todayâs example is far and away the most concerning development so far, because Iâm forced to admit that these AI-decompiled web browser ports of Call of Duty: Black Ops, Halo: CE, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Skate 3, and The Simpsons: Hit and Run actually seem to run very well.

Sure, lawyers for Take-Two and Microsoft and whoever else can send out some cease-and-desist letters and get these taken down. But then what? These browser ports were clearly easy and fast to create, so whatâs gonna stop people from just vibe-coding another version of these browser ports?

you can play Black Ops zombies, Skate 3, Halo and MW2 and more GAMES all run in a browser tab now. full list in the comments.

This is IP protection whack-a-mole on a scale I donât think weâve seen since the advent of pirated DVDs. I genuinely donât know how you put the genie back in the bottle on something like this. I played through a bunch of the web browser ports of the games linked in the thread above, and some of them seemed to be borderline flawless. In the case of The Simpsons: Hit and Run, it might even be better than flawless, because I donât remember the game being able to target 240fps when I was a kid. Itâs also extremely worrying that one of the four different web browser ports of Halo: CE I played had working online serversâ¦and my ping was low.

Look, Iâm not happy about admitting this, but itâs the truthâand itâs a pretty straightforward one at that. Most of the games that are being ported to browsers are PS2- or PS3-era titles. You know how much RAM the PS3 had? About 512 megabytes. You know how much memory my web browser is currently using as I type this? About 1,200 megabytes.

Web browser ports havenât been limited by RAM usage for quite some timeâthe difference here is that Claude Opus 5.5 is an AI you can leave running overnight to decompile a game instead of painstakingly working your way through the code, like your grandpappy used to.
I donât know where we go from here. All I can say with any certainty is that video game publishersâ legal teams are going to be working overtime for the foreseeable future.

articles.headline: After modders removed Skate's live service bits, devs draw the line with tools that "bypass our systems to unlock paid cosmetics"
keyFacts: Developer Full Circle stated they support player creativity in the early access game Skate, but object to mods bypassing systems to unlock paid cosmetics.
This response followed the popularity of the ReSkate modding platform, which gained hundreds of thousands of downloads to let players use the game offline.
Full Circle warned that unauthorized tools bypass monetization, while ReSkate creators stated they understand the need for game revenue.
body: EA and Full Circle - the developer behind the new early access Skate game (skate.) - don't have a problem with modders and "creativity from players," but they're drawing the line with mods that aim to unlock paid microtransactions and unreleased content.

This comes just days after modding platform ReSkate blew up big time, reaching 350,000 downloads in mere hours. ReSkate essentially lets players experience the skating sim revival completely offline, unlike the online-only base game, with custom maps and cosmetics and servers.

"Like many of you, we've been following the launch of numerous mods for our game. Skateboarding in general is built on community and creative expression, and we support that. We love seeing your passion for pushing the limits of San Vansterdam in different ways. That’s why we built our new skateboarding sandbox in San Vansterdam to begin with, to give you, the players, the tools you need to have fun and create amazing content," a developer statement posted to Reddit and other online forums said.

"To be completely clear, we are not against creativity from players or stopping that from happening. Where we have to draw the line is when mods or other tools bypass our systems to unlock paid cosmetics, release gated/unreleased content, or profit from these unauthorized assets. That rips off the artists, skate brands, and creators, as well as our own development team here at Full Circle, who work hard to bring skate culture into our game," the studio continued, before promising deeper community creation tools in the future.

Seems like Full Circle aren't taking action against ReSkate or any modders who are making their own fun stuff, for now, though the statement does seem like a warning of sorts to anyone trying to democratise the game's live service economy.

Speaking to PC Gamer, the coders responsible for ReSkate said they weren't trying to "replace the live game" and understood Full Circle needs "to make money somehow to be able to keep developing the game." ReSkate's official channels also don't allow mods that freely give access to premium cosmetics from the main game.

Full Circle ran into a bit of trouble earlier this year when the developer laid off an unspecified number of staff. Pro skaters have since slapped the sim with a Mixed Steam rating, with most complaints citing overbearing microtransactions and far too much paywalled content. Eurogamer's early access review liked Skate's - excuse me, skate.'s - initial version well enough.

articles.headline: AWS AgentCore security undone by prompt requesting credentials
keyFacts: Zenity Labs researchers discovered that AWS AgentCore allowed attackers to extract temporary credentials through a single chat prompt.
The flaw enabled attackers to hijack agents, access user session histories, and modify memory resources across an AWS account and region.
AWS fixed the vulnerabilities by September 2026, though Amazon later claimed Zenity's research misrepresented documented system behavior.
body: Bob, possibly the same Bob whose conversations with Alice draw so much interest from eavesdropping Eve, was browsing a site we'll call TechHub. The site hosts an AI agent served by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Bob asked the agent for help understanding the content of a URL, a credential endpoint – in raw JSON, if you don't mind. The endpoint returned data from the Instance Metadata Service (IMDS), which provides metadata about cloud instances and VMs at providers like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform. The metadata includes details like region and availability zone, subnets, system images, security groups, public keys injected during spawning, but also potentially more sensitive details like user data and security tokens. IMDSv2 addresses some of these risks, but back when Bob was browsing late last year, Bedrock AgentCore still used IMDSv1. The metadata provided to Bob by the helpful agent contained the agent's temporary credentials. So Bob loaded them onto his local machine, and remotely enumerated the company's other agents in that AWS region. He then logged into the Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR), pulled the agent container images, and ran each as root to inspect the source code. The stolen credentials also allowed Bob to discover the memory resources available in that AWS region, including the ones used by agents. From these, he's able to extract the users and their agent sessions – their conversations. Researchers at Zenity Labs disclosed their findings to AWS in December 2025. "We discovered that agents deployed through AgentCore could access their instance's IMDS endpoints," said Tamir Ishay Sharbat and Lana Salameh in a blog post. "This meant that an external attacker with nothing more than chat access to a single exposed agent could send a single prompt, extract its IMDS credentials, and use them to take over all AgentCore agents in the same AWS account and region." The basic problem, they explain, is that the Firecracker MicroVM used by AgentCore failed to provide sufficient network isolation. So an attacker – I know you're thinking it was Mallory, but it was really Bob – could direct the agent to carry out a server-side request forgery (SSRF) attack by fetching temporary AWS credentials for the IAM role assigned to the workload. And because the default AgentCore role was overpermissioned – it was scoped to all AgentCore resources in the region rather than a single agent – anyone in possession of the temporary IAM credentials could launch other agents, read sessions, write agent memories, and fetch secrets from AWS Secrets Manager. "By leveraging the IMDS credentials we could send direct API requests to create new memories across different agents and users," said Sharbat and Salameh. "These in turn would persistently alter agent behaviour and hijack the agents’ goals across future sessions." The Zenity researchers told Bob's tale, or something like it, to AWS last December, then followed up in January 2026 with details about AgentCore being overprivileged. On April 12, 2026, AWS responded to the security biz that its report was "informative" and closed the report, noting that as of February 14, 2026, AgentCore had been updated to use IMDSv2 exclusively. AgentCore's excessive permissions remained in place at least until June 22, 2026, when Zenity checked in and found the issue hadn't been remediated. A final review by Zenity occurred on September 29, 2026, at which point the biz observed that AWS had addressed the extant problems, clearing the way for Bob's hypothetical adventure to finally be told. Following publication, Amazon wrote in to say that Zenity’s research misrepresents documented behavior as a vulnerability, suggesting that developer error would be required to enable the attack. We’ve asked for clarification since that’s not the scenario Zenity has described. ®

articles.headline: 4 ways Amazon’s new Alexa tablets eclipse the Fire line – starting with Google Play
keyFacts: Amazon announced three new Alexa Tablets and two Kids' Tablets featuring Google Play support.
The devices start at $230 and feature aluminum construction with integrated Alexa+ AI.
The new Alexa Tablets are available for pre-order and will ship on October 14.
body: ZDNET’s key takeaways
- Three new Amazon Alexa tablets feature Alexa+ and premium construction, including a 12-inch Pro model.
- The tablets finally support Google Play, addressing a pain point for users.
- Amazon also launched two new Kids’ Tablets.

Amazon just announced three new Alexa Tablets, a trio of AI-powered Android tablets for work and entertainment with a more “Pro” build. The new tablets are an unexpected upgrade for Amazon, and an indication that the company is moving away from budget-focused tablets to more premium devices.
Also: 6 ways to make Android look and work more like iOS

The lineup starts at $230 and includes the Amazon Alexa Tablet 8, the Amazon Alexa Tablet 11 at $330, and the Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, which starts at $500. All three tablets are currently available for pre-order, and will start shipping on October 14.
More from ZDNET
1. Finally, Google Play access

Aside from being designed to work with Alexa+, the biggest change with these tablets is that they’re the first of the newer Amazon tablets to support access to Google Play, not just Amazon’s walled app store.

Amazon also announced a set of new Kids’ Tablets in bright colors and ready-to-go bundles with access to Google Play, though parents will still be able to control which apps their kids can access and download.
2. Alexa+ integrations everywhere

As the name indicates, the Alexa Tablets feature the Alexa+ virtual assistant integrated throughout. Instead of just having Alexa+ as a voice assistant, the new tablets feature the AI assistant woven into the interface, similar to how Gemini is for typical Android tablets.
The new Alexa Tablets can have Alexa interpret what is on your screen and answer questions about it. You can also have live, ongoing conversations without repeating the wake word before each one.
3. Completely new hardware

On the hardware side, the Alexa Tablets also feature a major upgrade. The Tablet 8 features 4GB of RAM and 64GB of storage for everyday use. The Tablet 11 has 8GB of RAM and 64GB of storage for extra entertainment and light work.
Most notably, though, the three tablets feature a more upscale aluminum design, which should feel like a considerable upgrade when compared to the older tablets’ plastic construction.
4. Pro-level performance and accessories

The Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, however, has a 4nm 8-core processor, 8GB or 16GB of RAM, and 128GB of storage. It also features a 12-inch display with a 120Hz refresh rate and comes with the option of a Nanomatte anti-glare display tablet for $50 more, starting at $550. You can also get a Pro Pen with the Pro tablet for $90, which supports 4,096 pressure levels, has tilt detection, and wireless charging.

Amazon also sells a Pro Keyboard for this flagship tablet, which is magnetic, features a trackpad, and requires no Bluetooth pairing. Instead of a simple iterative update, the new Alexa Tablets are an entirely redesigned lineup that could reposition Amazon tablets as full-fledged Android tablets.
New Amazon Kids Tablets

Amazon also launched two new, upgraded Kids Tablets: the Amazon Kids Tablet 8, starting at $230, and the Amazon Kids Tablet 11, starting at $330. The Kids’ tablets come in an 8.7-inch and 11-inch form factor, the latter of which has a 2.5K display and 8GB of RAM.

The Kids Tablets also feature Android instead of FireOS, improved hardware and screen resolution, AI-powered storytelling, and more convenient parental controls. Unfortunately, the Kids Tablets feature a one-year limited warranty, which is a considerable reduction from the previous tablets’ two-year, worry-free guarantee.
